children.text: jaiminīyagṛhyasūtram
children.translated_text: <s>Jaiminīya Gṛhya Sūtra</s> (The Domestic Ritual Sūtra of the <s>Jaiminīya</s> School)

children.text: JaimGS 1.1:
children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 1.1:

children.text: athāto 'gniṃ praṇoṣyanprāgudakpravaṇamabhyukṣya sthaṇiḍalaṃ lakṣaṇaṃ kuryānmadhye prācīṃ rekhāmullikhyodīcīṃ ca saṃhitāṃ paścāttisro madhye prācyo 'bhyukṣyāgniṃ pratiṣṭhāpayedbhūrbhuvaḥ svariti lakṣaṇāvṛdeṣā sarvatrāthātaḥ pākayajñānvyākhyāsyāmo huto 'hutaḥ prahutaḥ prāśita iti teṣāmekāgnau homo nitye yajñopavītodakācamane darśapūrṇamāsatantrāḥ snatantrā vā dakṣiṇato 'gneḥ pūrṇapātramupanidadhāti sruvaṃ cāpāṃ pūrṇamuttarato 'gneridhmābahirdevasya tvā savituḥ prasave 'śvinorbāhubhyāṃ pūṣṇo hastābhyāṃ prokṣāmiti prokṣitamupakḷptaṃ bhavati sakṛdyajuṣādvistūṣaṇiṃ khādiraḥ pālāśo vedhmastadalābhe vibhītakatilvakabādhakanimbarājavṛjñaśalmalyaraludadhitthakovidāraśrleṣmātakavarjaṃ sarvavanaspatīnāmidhmaḥ kuśālābhe śūkatṛṇaśaraśīryabalbajamutavanalaśuṇṭhavarjaṃ sarvatṛṇāniśuklāḥ sumanasastāsāmalābhe japārupakākutthābhaṇḍīkuraṇḍakavarjaṃ gandhavatyo vā sarvavarṇāścatasr ājyaprakṛtayo bhavantyūdhanyaṃ vā vāhyaṃ vā payo vā paścādagnerācamanaṃ trirācāmeddviḥ parimṛjetsapṛdupaspṛśetpādāvabhyukṣya śiraśca śīṣaṇyānprāṇānupaspṛśedarpaupaspṛśya paścādagnerupasamāhitasyopaviśya dakṣiṇena pāṇinābhūmimārabhya japatīdaṃ bhūmerbhajāmaha idaṃ bhadraṃ sumaṅgalaṃ parā sapantānbādhasvānyeṣāṃ vinda te dhanamiti vasvantaṃ rātriścedimaṃstomyena tṛcenāgniṃ parisamūhedādyayā vā triḥ prastaramupasaṃgṛhya pratidiśaṃ paristṛṇāti dakṣiṇapurastādupakramyāgrairmūlāni chādayanpaścādvopastīryolaparājibhyāmupahareddakṣiṇottaraḥ sandhiḥ // JaimGS_1.1 //
children.translated_text: Now, when about to lead the fire forward, having sprinkled [the ground] on a surface sloping toward the east and north, one should make the markings on the <s>sthaṇḍila</s> (ground-altar): having drawn an eastward line in the middle and a northward line joined to it, then three eastward lines in the middle behind; having sprinkled, one should establish the fire with '<s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>.' This marking procedure applies everywhere. Now, we shall explain the <s>pākayajñas</s> (cooked offerings): the <s>huta</s> (offered), the <s>ahuta</s> (not-offered), the <s>prahuta</s> (cast), and the <s>prāśita</s> (eaten). Of these, the oblation is in a single fire. The <s>yajñopavīta</s> (sacred thread) and <s>ācamana</s> (water-sipping) are constant. They follow the pattern of the <s>darśa-pūrṇamāsa</s> (new-moon and full-moon rites), or the pattern of the <s>snāna</s> (bathing ceremony). To the south of the fire, one places a full vessel and a <s>sruva</s> (ladle) full of water. To the north of the fire, the fuel-sticks are placed outside. With [the words] 'At the impulsion of god <s>Savitṛ</s>, with the arms of the <s>Aśvins</s>, with the hands of <s>Pūṣan</s>, I sprinkle you' — what is sprinkled becomes ritually prepared. Once with the <s>Yajus</s> formula, twice silently. The <s>idhma</s> (fuel-stick) should be of <s>khadira</s> (acacia), <s>palāśa</s> (butea), or <s>vedhma</s>; in the absence of these, the fuel may be from any forest tree except <s>vibhītaka</s>, <s>tilvaka</s>, <s>bādhaka</s>, <s>nimba</s> (neem), <s>rājavṛkṣa</s>, <s>śalmali</s> (silk-cotton), <s>aralu</s>, <s>udadhittha</s>, <s>kovidāra</s>, and <s>śleṣmātaka</s>. In the absence of <s>kuśa</s> grass, any grass may be used except <s>śūka</s>, <s>tṛṇa-śara</s>, <s>śīrya</s>, <s>balbaja</s>, <s>muta</s>, <s>vanala</s>, and <s>śuṇṭha</s>. White <s>sumanas</s> (jasmine) flowers [are used]; in their absence, any fragrant flower of any color may be used, except <s>japā</s> (hibiscus), <s>rupaka</s>, <s>ākuttha</s>, <s>bhaṇḍī</s>, and <s>kuraṇḍaka</s>. The four base substances for <s>ājya</s> (clarified butter) are: <s>ūdhanya</s> (fresh from the udder), <s>vāhya</s> (drawn), or <s>payas</s> (milk). After the fire, one performs <s>ācamana</s>: one sips three times, wipes twice, touches with a moist hand, sprinkles the feet and the head, touches the sense organs at the head, touches water again; then, sitting behind the fire in a composed manner, touching the earth with the right hand, one recites: 'We share in this [bounty] of the earth; this is auspicious, of good omen; drive away those who are hostile; find wealth for others' — ending with <s>vasu</s>. If it is nighttime, one sweeps around the fire with the <s>stomya</s> three-versed hymn, or with the first [verse] three times. Having taken up the <s>prastara</s> (grass-bundle), one strews it in each direction, beginning from the southeast, covering the roots with the tips; or having strewn it behind, one offers the <s>ūlaparāji</s> oblations. The junction [of the grass strewn] from south to north [completes the procedure]. // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.1 //

children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 1.2:

children.text: prastarātpavitre gṛhṇāti prādeśamātre same apraśīrṇāgre anantargarbhe aṅguṣṭhenopakāniṣṭhikayā ca dhārayannanakhena chinatti pavitre stho vaiṣṇavyāviti trirurdhavamadbhiranumārjayedviṣaṇormanasā pūte stha iti sakṛdyajuṣā dvistūṣṇīṃ pātrasyopariṣṭātpavitre dhārayannājyamāsicyottareṇāgnimaṅgārātriruhya teṣvadhiśrityāvadyotya darbhataruṇābhyāṃ pratyasya triḥparyagni kṛtvodagudvāsya pratyūhyāṅgārānudagagrābhyāṃ pavitrābhyāṃ trirutpunātyājyaṃ ca haviśca praṇītāśca sruvaṃ ca devastvā savitotpunātvacchidreṇa pavitreṇa vasoḥ sūryasya raśmibhiriti devo va iti praṇītāḥ punarāhāramājyasya sakṛdyajuṣā dvistūṣṇīmuttarato 'gneḥ praṇītāḥ praṇīya darbhaiḥ pracchādya dakṣiṇato 'gneḥ prastaraṃ nidhāya prastarasyopariṣṭātpavitre nidhāya virupākṣaṃ japatyoṃ tapaśca satyaṃ cātmā ca dhṛtiśca dharmaśca sattavaṃ ca tyāgaśca brahma ca brahma ca tāni prapadye tāni māmavantu bhūrbhuvaḥ svaroṃ mahāntamātmānamadhyārohāmi virupākṣo 'si dantājjistasya te śayyā parṇe gṛhā antarikṣe te vimitaṃ hiraṇmayaṃ taddevānāṃ hṛdayānyayasmaye kumbhe antaḥ saṃnihitāni tāni balabhūśca baladhā ca rakṣaṇo mā pramadaḥ satyaṃ te dvādaśa putrāste tvā saṃvatsaresaṃvatsare kāmapreṇa yajñena yājayitvā punarbrahmacaryamupayanti tvaṃ devānāṃ brāhmaṇo 'syahaṃ manuṣyāṇāṃ brāhmaṇo vai brāhmaṇāmupadhāvati taṃ tvopadhāvāmi japantaṃ mā mā pratijāpsīrjuhvantaṃ mā mā pratihauṣīḥ kurvantaṃ mā mā pratikārṣīstvāṃ prapadde tvayā prasūta idaṃ karma kariṣyāmi tanme samṛdhyatāṃ virupākṣāya dantājjaye brahmaṇāḥ putrāya jyeṣṭhāya śreṣṭhāyāmodhāya karmādhipataye nama iti // JaimGS_1.2 //
children.translated_text: From the <s>prastara</s> (grass-bundle), one takes the two <s>pavitras</s> (purifying blades): a span in length, even, with unbroken tips, without inner pith, holding them with the thumb and the little finger, and cutting them without using the nail. [Saying] 'You are <s>pavitras</s>, belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — one wipes them upward with water three times. [Saying] 'You are purified by the mind of <s>Viṣṇu</s>' — once with the <s>Yajus</s> formula, twice silently. Holding the <s>pavitras</s> over the vessel, one pours in the <s>ājya</s> (clarified butter); north of the fire, having climbed over the embers, having placed [the vessel] on them, having melted [the ājya], having pushed aside [impurities] with two fresh <s>darbha</s> blades, having circled the fire three times, having removed it northward, having pushed back the embers — with the two <s>pavitras</s> whose tips point northward, one purifies three times the <s>ājya</s>, the <s>havis</s> (oblation), the <s>praṇītā</s> waters, and the <s>sruva</s> (ladle), [saying] 'May god <s>Savitṛ</s> purify you with the flawless <s>pavitra</s>, with the rays of <s>Vasu Sūrya</s>' — [and for] the <s>praṇītā</s> waters, 'O god <s>Vasu</s>.' One again takes up a portion of <s>ājya</s>, once with the <s>Yajus</s>, twice silently. North of the fire, having carried the <s>praṇītā</s> waters forward, having covered them with <s>darbha</s> grass, having placed the <s>prastara</s> to the south of the fire, having placed the two <s>pavitras</s> on top of the <s>prastara</s>, one recites the <s>Virupākṣa</s> [prayer]: '<s>Oṃ</s>, <s>tapas</s> (austerity) and truth, the self, fortitude, <s>dharma</s>, goodness, renunciation, <s>Brahman</s> — <s>Brahman</s>: I take refuge in these; may these protect me. <s>Bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>. <s>Oṃ</s>, I ascend upon the great Self. You are <s>Virupākṣa</s>. Your couch is from tusks. Your dwellings are in leaves. In the atmosphere is your golden pavilion measured out. Those are the hearts of the gods, deposited within an iron vessel. May <s>Balabhū</s>, <s>Baladhā</s>, and <s>Rakṣaṇa</s> [protect]. Let there be no negligence. Truth is yours. Your twelve sons, having caused you to sacrifice year after year with the desire-fulfilling sacrifice, enter <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy) again. You are the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of the gods; I am the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> of humans. Indeed, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> approaches a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. I approach you. Do not hinder me as I recite! Do not obstruct me as I offer! Do not impede me as I act! I take refuge in you. Impelled by you, I shall perform this rite. May it succeed for me. Homage to <s>Virupākṣa Dantājjaya</s>, the son of <s>Brahman</s>, the eldest, the best, the infallible, the lord of rites.' // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.2 //

children.text: JaimGS 1.3:
children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 1.3:

children.text: sruvaṃ praṇītāsu praṇīya niṣṭapya darbhaiḥ saṃmṛjya saṃmārgānabhyukṣyāgnāvādhāya dakṣiṇāṃ jānvācyāmedhyaṃ cetkiṃcidājye 'vapadyeta ghuṇāstryambukā makṣikā pipīliketyā pañcabhya ḥddhatyābhyukṣyotpūya jūhuyātparitadhinparidadhāti madhyamaṃ sthavīyasaṃ paścāddīrdhaṃ madhyamaṃ dakṣiṇātaḥ kanīyasamuttarataḥ saṃspṛṣṭāndakṣiṇāto 'gnerapāṃ kośaṃ ninayatyadite 'numanyasvetyanumate 'nmanyasveti paścātsarasvate 'numanyasvetyuttarato deva savitaḥ prasuveti triḥ pradakṣiṇamagniṃ pariṣiñceddeva savitaḥ prasuva yajñaṃ prasuva yajñapatiṃ bhagāya divyo gandharvaḥ ketapūḥ ketaṃ naḥ punātu vācaspatirvācaṃ naḥ svadatviti sakṛdyajuṣā dvistūṣṇīmathedhmamādāya sruveṇājyaṃ gṛhītvābhighāryāgnāvabhyādadhātyayaṃ ta idhma ātmā jātavedastena vardhasva cedhyasva cendvi vardhaya cāsmānprajayā paśubhirbrahmavarcasenānnādyena samedhaya svāheti manasāghārau juhoti saṃtatamakṣṇāyā prajāpataye svāhetyuttaraṃ paridhisandhimanvavahṛtya sruvamundrāya svāheti dakṣiṇāṃ paridhisandhimanvavahṛtyāghārau hutvājyabhāgau juhotyagnaye svāhetyattarataḥ somāya svāheti dakṣiṇatastāvantareṇāhutiloko bhūḥ svāhā bhuvaḥ svāhā svaḥ svāhā bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhetyagnaye 'gnīṣomābhyāmiti paurṇamāsāsyāmagnaya indrāgnibhyāmityamāvāsyāyāmuttarapūrvāma uttarapūrvāmāhutiṃ juhotyanabhijuhvadāhutyāhutiṃ pratyak sauviṣṭakṛtasthānānnityo 'gniḥ purastātsviṣṭakṛdante 'nyatra vapāhomājyahomābhyāṃ na sviṣṭakṛtaṃ pratyabhighārayati sruve sakṛdājyamupastṛṇāti dvirhaviṣo 'vadyati dvisakṛdājyonābhighārya pratyabhidhā rayatyāṅguṣṭhenāṅgulibhyāṃ ca māṃsasaṃhitābhyāṃ dvarhaviṣo 'vadyati dvirājyenābhidhārya pratyabhighārayati jāmadagnyānāṃ tadvi pancāvattaṃ bhavatyaṅgulyā tṛṇakūrcena vā eṣā homāvṛtsarvatra // JaimGS_1.3 //
children.translated_text: Having placed the <s>sruva</s> (ladle) in the <s>praṇītā</s> waters, having dipped it, having wiped it with <s>darbha</s> grass, having sprinkled the wiping-grass, having placed it on the fire — one bends the right knee. If something impure falls into the <s>ājya</s> — a worm, a <s>tryambuka</s> (three-eyed insect), a fly, or an ant — one removes it from those five [types], sprinkles, purifies again, and offers. One places the <s>paridhi</s> (enclosing sticks): the middle one being the thickest, the one behind being long and medium, the southern one smaller, and the northern one. They should be touching. To the south of the fire, one pours out the water-vessel, [saying] '<s>Aditi</s>, give your consent!' — 'O <s>Anumatī</s>, give your consent!' behind — 'O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, give your consent!' to the north — 'O god <s>Savitṛ</s>, impel!' One circumambulates the fire three times clockwise, sprinkling: 'O god <s>Savitṛ</s>, impel the sacrifice, impel the lord of the sacrifice, for [our] share. May the divine <s>gandharva Ketapū</s> purify our intention. May <s>Vācaspati</s> (Lord of Speech) make our speech agreeable.' Once with the <s>Yajus</s>, twice silently. Then, taking the fuel-stick and having taken <s>ājya</s> with the <s>sruva</s>, having anointed it, one places it on the fire: 'This is your fuel, O <s>Jātavedas</s> (knower of births). By it, may you grow and thrive. May <s>Indra</s> increase. And increase us with offspring, cattle, <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual radiance), and food. Prosper [us], <s>svāhā</s>!' One offers the two <s>āghāra</s> (preliminary) oblations mentally in an unbroken stream, obliquely: '<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Prajāpati</s>!' — carrying the oblation along the northern <s>paridhi</s>-junction. '<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Indra</s>!' — carrying it along the southern <s>paridhi</s>-junction. Having offered the two <s>āghāras</s>, one offers the two <s>ājyabhāgas</s> (butter-portions): '<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Agni</s>!' to the north; '<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Soma</s>!' to the south. Between these [one offers] the principal oblation. '<s>Bhūḥ svāhā</s>, <s>bhuvaḥ svāhā</s>, <s>svaḥ svāhā</s>, <s>bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhā</s>!' For the full-moon [rite], [the oblation is] to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Agni-Soma</s>; for the new-moon [rite], to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Indra-Agni</s>. One offers each subsequent oblation after the preceding one. Without offering additionally, [one proceeds] from the oblation-place to the place of <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> (the 'making-right' oblation) inversely. The constant fire [oblation goes] before. The <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s> comes at the end, except in the case of the <s>vapā-homa</s> (omentum oblation) and <s>ājya-homa</s>. One does not re-anoint after the <s>sviṣṭakṛt</s>. In the <s>sruva</s>, one strews <s>ājya</s> once, cuts the <s>havis</s> twice, anoints with <s>ājya</s> twice and once, and re-anoints. With the thumb and the two fingers together with the flesh, one cuts the <s>havis</s> twice, anoints with <s>ājya</s> twice, and re-anoints. According to the <s>Jāmadagnya</s> tradition, this is done fivefold — [or] with the finger, or with a bunch of grass. This is the oblation procedure everywhere. // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.3 //

children.text: JaimGS 1.4:
children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 1.4:

children.text: sapavitraṃ prastaramādatte tasyāgrāṇi sruve 'nakti divyaṅkṣveti madhyamājye 'ntarikṣe 'ṅkṣveti mūlāni haviṣi pṛthivyāmaṅkṣvavati prastarāttṛṇaṃ nirasyatyāyuṣe tveti prastaramagnāvanupraharatyagnaye 'numataye svāheti paścāttṛṇamanupraharati dviṣantaṃ me 'bhidhehi taṃ caiva pradaha svāheti ghṛtenāktāḥ samidha ādadhāti samṛddhyai svāheti bhūmimārabhya śīrṣaṇyānprāṇānupaspṛśedapa upaspṛśya dvādaśa prāyaścittāhutīrjuhotyākūtyai svāhā //
children.translated_text: One takes up the <s>prastara</s> (grass-bundle) together with the <s>pavitras</s>. One anoints the tips of the <s>prastara</s> in the <s>sruva</s>, [saying] 'Be anointed in heaven!' — the middle portion in the <s>ājya</s>, [saying] 'Be anointed in the atmosphere!' — the roots in the <s>havis</s>, [saying] 'Be anointed on earth!' One removes a blade from the <s>prastara</s>, [saying] 'For long life!' One casts the <s>prastara</s> into the fire, [saying] '<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Agni Anumati</s>!' One casts the blade behind, [saying] 'Strike my enemy; burn that one too, <s>svāhā</s>!' One places fuel-sticks anointed with ghee, [saying] 'For prosperity, <s>svāhā</s>!' Touching the earth, one touches the sense-organs at the head; touching water, one offers twelve <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) oblations: '<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Ākūti</s> (intention)!'

children.text: kāmāya svāhā //
children.translated_text: '<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Kāma</s> (desire)!'

children.text: samṛddhayai svāhā //
children.translated_text: '<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Samṛddhi</s> (prosperity)!'

children.text: ṛcā stomaṃ samardhaya gāyatreṇa rathaṃtaraṃ bṛhadgāyatravartani svāhā //
children.translated_text: 'Fulfill the <s>stoma</s> (hymn of praise) with the <s>Ṛc</s> verse, the <s>Rathaṃtara</s> [<s>Sāman</s>] with the <s>Gāyatra</s>, the <s>Bṛhat</s> with the <s>Gāyatra</s> meter, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: udu tyaṃ jātavedasaṃ devaṃ vahanti ketavaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The rays carry up that newborn god <s>Jātavedas</s>,

children.text: d daśe viśvāya sūryaṃ svāhā //
children.translated_text: the sun visible to all, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: citraṃ devānāmudagādanīkaṃ cakṣurmitrasya varuṇasyāgneḥ /
children.translated_text: 'The wondrous face of the gods has risen, the eye of <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Agni</s>;

children.text: āprā dyāvāpṛthivī antarikṣaṃ sūrya ātmā jagatastasthuṣaśca svāhā //
children.translated_text: <s>Sūrya</s> has filled heaven, earth, and the atmosphere — <s>Sūrya</s> is the self of all that moves and stands, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: udvayaṃ tamasaspari svaḥ paśyanto jyotirūttaram /
children.translated_text: 'Upward, beyond the darkness, beholding the higher light,

children.text: devaṃ devatrā sūryamaganma jyotirūttamaṃ svāhā //
children.translated_text: we have reached <s>Sūrya</s>, the god among gods, the supreme light, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: prajāpate na tvadetānyanyo viśvā jātāni pari tā babhūva /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Prajāpati</s>, no other than you has encompassed all these created beings;

children.text: yatkāmāste juhumastanno 'stu vayaṃ syāma patayo rayīṇāṃ svāhā //
children.translated_text: may that for which we offer oblations be ours — may we be lords of riches, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: bhūḥ svāhā //
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhūḥ svāhā</s>!'

children.text: bhuvaḥ svāhā //
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhuvaḥ svāhā</s>!'

children.text: svaḥ svāhā //
children.translated_text: '<s>Svaḥ svāhā</s>!'

children.text: bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ svāhetyathāstīrṇāndarbhānānīya praṇītānāṃ ca sruvasya copariṣṭātkṛtvāpastrāvayañjapati sadasi sanme bhūyāḥ sarvamasi sarvaṃ me bhūyāḥ pūrṇamasi pūrṇaṃ me bhūyā akṣitamasi mā me kṣeṣṭhā iti pratidiśamapa utsiñcati prācyāṃ diśi devā ṛtvijo mārjayantāmiti prācīnāvītī dakṣiṇāsyāṃ diśi māsāḥ pitaro mārjayantāmiti yajñopavītī bhūtvāpa upaspṛśya pratīcyāṃ diśi gṛhāḥ paśavo mārjayantāmityudīcyāṃ diśyāpa oṣadhayo vanaspatayo mārjayantāmityūdhvāyāṃ diśi yajñaḥ saṃvatsaro yajñapatirmārjayantāmiti samudraṃ vaḥ prahiṇomītyapo ninīya samudraṃ vaḥ prahiṇobhyakṣitāḥ svāṃ yonimapi gacchata /
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>, <s>svāhā</s> — thus, having brought the spread <s>darbha</s> grasses and having placed [them] above the consecrated waters and the ladle, while straining the water he recites: 'Being in the assembly, may you be for me; you are everything, may you be everything for me; you are full, may you be full for me; you are imperishable, may you not perish for me.' Thus he pours out water in each direction: in the eastern direction [he says] 'May the gods and the <s>ṛtvijs</s> (priests) purify!' — [reciting this] with the sacred thread over the right shoulder (<s>prācīnāvītī</s>); in the southern direction, 'May the months and the <s>pitṛs</s> (ancestors) purify!' — having put on the sacred thread in the normal manner (<s>yajñopavītī</s>) and touching water; in the western direction, 'May the households and cattle purify!'; in the northern direction, 'May the waters, herbs, and trees purify!'; in the upward direction, 'May the sacrifice, the year, and the lord of sacrifice purify!' 'I send you to the ocean' — thus having led away the waters — 'I send you to the ocean; imperishable, go to your own source!'

children.text: ariṣṭā asmākaṃ vīrāḥ santu mā parāseci naḥ svamiti yadapsu te sarasvatītyaṅguṣṭhenopakaniṣṭhikayā cākṣiṇī vimṛjedyadapsu te sarasvati goṣvaśveṣu yanmadhu /
children.translated_text: 'May our heroes be unharmed; do not pour away what is ours' — thus, [reciting] 'That which is in the waters, O <s>Sarasvatī</s>,' with the thumb and the ring finger he should wipe both eyes — 'That which is in the waters, O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, that honey which is in cows and horses' —

children.text: tena me vājināvati mukhamaṅdhi sarasvatīti darbhānparidhīṃścāgnāvādhāya vāmadevyena śāntiṃ kṛtvā triḥ paryukṣetsahaviṣkaṃ pradakṣiṇamanvamaṃsthāḥ prāsāvīriti mantrānsaṃnamayetpūrṇapātramupanihitaṃ sā dakṣiṇā yathāśraddhadakṣiṇāḥ pākayajñāḥ pūrṇapātraṃ vā // JaimGS_1.4 //
children.translated_text: 'With that, O prize-winning <s>Sarasvatī</s>, anoint my face' — thus, having placed the <s>darbha</s> grasses and the enclosing sticks in the fire, having performed the <s>śānti</s> (peace invocation) with the <s>Vāmadevya</s> [<s>Sāman</s>], he should sprinkle three times together with the oblation. 'You have circumambulated; you have generated' — thus he should conclude the <s>mantras</s> reverentially. A full vessel placed nearby — that is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). The fees are according to one's faith. For <s>pākayajñas</s> (cooked-food offerings), a full vessel [is the fee]. // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.4 //

children.text: JaimGS 1.5:
children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 1.5:

children.text: puṃsavanaṃ tṛtīyo māsyanyatra gṛṣṭerghṛte caruṃ śrapayitvā pṛṣadājyaṃ vā sthālīpākavatsaṃskṛtya pūruṣasūktena juhuyānmāṣau ca yavaṃ ca pulliṅgaṃ kṛtvā dadhidrapsenaināṃ prāśayetprajāpatiḥ puruṣaḥ parameṣṭhi sa me putraṃ dadātvāyuṣmantaṃ yaṣasvinaṃ saha patyā jīvasūrbhūyāsamiti nyagrodhaśuṅgaṃ phalābhyāmupahitaṃ śuklaratkābhyāṃ sūtrābhyāṃ grathitvā kaṇṭhe dhārayeddhruvakumārāyetyācakṣate vāso dakṣiṇā // JaimGS_1.5 //
children.translated_text: The <s>puṃsavana</s> (rite for obtaining a male child) [is performed] in the third month, except for a woman who has already given birth. Having cooked an oblation (<s>caru</s>) in ghee, or [using] curds mixed with ghee (<s>pṛṣadājya</s>), having prepared it in the manner of a <s>sthālīpāka</s> offering, he should offer oblations with the <s>Puruṣa Sūkta</s>. Having made a male figure out of <s>māṣa</s> beans and barley, he should make her eat it with a drop of curds, [reciting:] 'May <s>Prajāpati</s>, the supreme <s>Puruṣa</s>, <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>, give me a son endowed with long life and fame; together with my husband, may I be a mother of living children.' Thus, a shoot of the banyan tree (<s>nyagrodha</s>) joined with two fruits, having been tied with white and red threads, she should wear it around her neck. They say this is for the 'steadfast child' (<s>dhruva-kumāra</s>). A garment is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>. // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.5 //

children.text: JaimGS 1.6:
children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 1.6:

children.text: athāto nāndīmukhebhyaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ pūrveddurvyākhyāsyāma āpūryamāṇapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre śvaḥ kariṣyamīti śvo bhūte vānnaṃ saṃskṛtyaśucīn śrotriyānbrāhmaṇānanumantrayate śuciḥ śuklamanārdramācchādya yajñopavītyapa ācamya catuḥśuklānbalīnharatī dadhi taṇḍulāḥ surabhi śuklāḥ sumanasa ityagnyāyatane prāgagrāndarbhānsaṃstīryāgnaye somāya prajāpataye viśvebhyo devebhya ṛṣibhyo bhūtyebhyaḥ pitṛbhyaḥ sarvābhyo devatābhyo nama iti haviṣyamannaṃ brāhmaṇobhyaḥ pradāya dadhrā māṣamatsyamāṃsabhakṣyāśanairityaparamatha catuṣṭayamādāya vrīhiyavapuṣpasarṣapāṇīti saha tairevodakumbhamādāya manaḥ samādhīyaṃtāṃ prasīdantu bhavanta ityutkā sapraṇavaṃ nāndīmukhāḥ pitaraḥ prīyantāmityevaṃ yathārthamitare pratibrūyuḥ // JaimGS_1.6 //
children.translated_text: Now therefore we shall explain in due order the [rites] for the <s>nāndīmukha</s> ancestors. In the waxing fortnight, on an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s> (asterism), [he announces] 'I shall perform it tomorrow.' When the morrow has come, having prepared the food, he invites pure, Veda-learned <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. Being ritually pure, having covered [himself] with a white, dry garment, wearing the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavīta</s>), having sipped water (<s>ācamana</s>), he brings four white offerings: curds, rice, fragrant [substances], and white flowers. Having strewn <s>darbha</s> grasses with tips pointing east at the fire-altar, [he recites:] 'Homage to <s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the <s>Ṛṣis</s>, the <s>Bhūtyas</s>, the <s>Pitṛs</s>, and all deities.' Thus, having given the sacrificial food to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, [he serves them] with curds, <s>māṣa</s> beans, fish, meat, and other eatables. Then, taking the fourfold [set] — rice, barley, flowers, and mustard seeds — together with these, taking a water-jar, [he says:] 'May the minds be concentrated; may the venerable ones be pleased.' Standing, with the <s>praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>), [he recites:] 'May the <s>nāndīmukha</s> ancestors be pleased' — thus the others should respond accordingly. // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.6 //

children.text: JaimGS 1.7:
children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 1.7:

children.text: sīmantonnayanaṃ caturthe māsi ṣaṣṭhe 'ṣṭame vā pūrvapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre hastottarābhirvā kuryāttilamudgamiśraṃ sthālīpākaṃ śrapayitvānvārabdhāyāṃ juhuyānmahāvyāhṛtibhirhutvā prājāpatyayā cāthaināṃ paścādagnerbhadrapīṭha upaveśyairakāyāṃ vāhatottarāyāṃ tasyai triḥ śuklayā śalalyā prāṇasaṃmitaṃ sīmaṃntaṃ kuryācchuklenā mūrdhraḥ prāṇāya tvāpānāya tvetyathāsyā dakṣiṇaṃ keśāntaṃ sragbhiralaṃkṛtya tathottaraṃ hiraṇyavatīnāmapāṃ kāṃsyaṃ pūrayitvā tatraināmavekṣayanpṛccheddhiṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ kiṃ paśyasīti parā pratyāha prajāṃ paśūnsaubhāgyaṃ mahyaṃ dīrghamāyuḥ patyuriti vāso dakṣiṇā hiraṇyaṃ vā // JaimGS_1.7 //
children.translated_text: The <s>sīmantonnayaṇa</s> (hair-parting ceremony) [is performed] in the fourth month, or in the sixth or eighth, in the waxing fortnight, on an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s>, or under the <s>Hasta</s> or <s>Uttarā</s> asterisms. Having cooked a <s>sthālīpāka</s> mixed with sesame and green gram, when [the wife] has grasped [the performer from behind], he should offer oblations. Having offered with the <s>mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great sacred utterances), and with the verse to <s>Prajāpati</s>, then he should seat her behind the fire on an auspicious seat, or on <s>erakā</s> grass [facing] north. For her, three times with a white porcupine quill, he should make the hair-parting extending the full length, with a white [quill] from the head, [reciting:] 'For <s>prāṇa</s>, for you; for <s>apāna</s>, for you.' Then, having adorned the right side of her hair with garlands, and likewise the left, having filled a bronze vessel with water containing gold, having her gaze into it, he should ask: '<s>Dhiṃ</s>! <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>! What do you see?' She replies: 'Offspring, cattle, good fortune for me, and long life for my husband.' A garment is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s>, or gold. // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.7 //

children.text: JaimGS 1.8:
children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 1.8:

children.text: kumāre jāte jātakarma prākstanaprāśanāhrīhiṃ ca yavaṃ ca jātarūpeṇāvaghṛṣyedamannamiti prāśayedidamannamayaṃ rasa idaṃ prāṇenāmṛtaṃ saha pṛthivī te mātā dyauḥ pitā jīvāhi śaradaḥ śataṃ paśyāhi śaradaḥ śatamityathainamabhimantrayate 'ṅgādaṅgātsaṃbhavasi hṛdayādadhi jāyase /
children.translated_text: When the child is born, the <s>jātakarma</s> (birth rite) [is performed] before the first feeding. Having ground rice and barley with gold, [reciting] 'This is food,' he should feed [the child]: 'This is food, this is essence, this is immortality together with the breath. The earth is your mother, heaven is your father. May you live a hundred autumns, may you see a hundred autumns.' Then he addresses the child with the <s>mantra</s>: 'From limb to limb you have come into being, from the heart you are born;

children.text: ātmā vai putranāmāsi sa jīva śaradaḥ śataṃ paśyāhi śaradaḥ śatamityathainaṃ paridadātyahno tvā paridadāmyahastvā rātryai paridadātu rātristvāhorātrābhyāṃ paridadātvahorātrau tvārdhamāsebhyaḥ paridattāmardhamāsāstvā māsebhyaḥ paridadatu māsāstvartubhyaḥ paridadattvṛtastvā saṃvatsarāya paridadatu saṃvatsarastvā jarāyai mṛtyave paridadātviti ko 'si katamo 'sītyāha saṃ māsaṃ praviśāsāvityathāsya guhyaṃ nāma dadāti vedo 'sītyathāsya mūrdhānamupajighratyaśmā bhava paraśurbhava hiraṇayamastṛtaṃ bhava paśūnāṃ tvā hiṃkāreṇābhijighrāmītyevameva pravāsādetya putrāṇāṃ mūrdhānamupajighrati phalīkaraṇamiśrānsarṣapāndaśarātramagnau juhuyāt śaṇaḍāyeti dvābhyāṃ śaṇaḍāya markāyopavīrāya śauṇḍikera ulūkhalo malimluco duṇāśi cyavano naśyatāditaḥ svāhā /
children.translated_text: You are indeed the self called "son." Live a hundred autumns, see a hundred autumns.' Then he hands [the child] over: 'I hand you over to the day; may the day hand you over to the night; may the night hand you over to the days-and-nights; may the days-and-nights hand you over to the half-months; may the half-months hand you over to the months; may the months hand you over to the seasons; may the seasons hand you over to the year; may the year hand you over to old age and death.' [He asks:] 'Who are you? Which one are you?' He says: 'Enter safely, O [name]!' Then he gives him a secret name: 'You are the <s>Veda</s>.' Then he smells the top of his head: 'Be a stone, be an axe, be uncut gold. I smell you with the <s>hiṃkāra</s> (lowing sound) of cattle.' In the same manner, upon returning from a journey, he smells the heads of his sons. He should offer mustard seeds mixed with parched rice into the fire for ten nights, [reciting:] 'To <s>Śaṇaḍa</s>' — with two [repetitions] — 'To <s>Śaṇaḍa</s>, to <s>Marka</s>, to <s>Upavīra</s>, O <s>Śauṇḍikera</s>, <s>Ulūkhala</s>, <s>Malimluca</s>, <s>Duṇāśi</s>, <s>Cyavana</s> — let them perish from here! <s>Svāhā</s>!'

children.text: ālikhanvilikhannanimiṣan kiṃvadanta upaśrutiraryamṇaḥ kumbhī śatruḥ pātrapāṇirnipuṇahāntrīmukhaḥ sarṣapārūṇo naśyatāditaḥ svāheti daśarātraṃ dampati sūtakau bhavatastasyānte snātvotthānam // JaimGS_1.8 //
children.translated_text: '<s>Ālikhan</s> (the scratcher), <s>Vilikhan</s> (the scribbler), <s>Animiṣan</s> (the unblinking), <s>Kiṃvadanta</s> (the whisperer), <s>Upaśruti</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>'s <s>Kumbhī</s>, <s>Śatru</s> (the enemy), <s>Pātrapāṇi</s> (the bowl-handed), <s>Nipuṇahāntrīmukha</s> (the cunning-mouthed), <s>Sarṣapārūṇa</s> — let them perish from here! <s>Svāhā</s>!' For ten nights the couple observes birth-impurity (<s>sūtaka</s>). At its end, having bathed, they arise [from the period of impurity]. // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.8 //

children.text: JaimGS 1.9:
children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 1.9:

children.text: athāto nāmakarma pūrvapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre dvādaśayāṃ vā pitā nāma kuryādācāryo vā pitā nāma kuryādācāryo vā tamahatena vāsasā samanuparigṛhya pitāṅgenāsīta tasya nāmadheyaṃ dadyād dvyakṣaraṃ caturakkṣaraṃ vā ghoṣavadādyantarantasthamanunakṣatramanudaivatanunāmātaddhitamākārāntaṃ striyai yathārthaṃ vā kumārayajñeṣu ca nakṣatraṃ nakṣatradaivataṃ tithimiti yajate 'ṣṭāvanyā juṣṭā devatā yajate 'gni dhanvantari prajāpatimindraṃ vasūntrudrānādityānviśvāndevānityetāsu sviṣṭāsu sarvā devatā abhīṣṭā bhavanti // JaimGS_1.9 //
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>nāmakarma</s> (naming ceremony). In the waxing fortnight, on an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s>, or on the twelfth day, the father should give the name, or the teacher. Having wrapped the child in a new garment, the father should sit with the child on his lap. He should give him a name of two or four syllables, having sonant consonants at the beginning and end, with semivowels in the middle, following the <s>nakṣatra</s>, following the deity, a derived name with a secondary suffix (<s>taddhita</s>), ending in <s>ā</s> for a girl, or a meaningful name. In the child's rituals, [one worships] the <s>nakṣatra</s>, the deity of the <s>nakṣatra</s>, and the lunar day (<s>tithi</s>) — thus he worships. He worships eight other beloved deities: <s>Agni</s>, <s>Dhanvantari</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Indra</s>, the <s>Vasus</s>, the <s>Rudras</s>, the <s>Ādityas</s>, and the <s>Viśvedevas</s>. When these are properly offered to, all deities are satisfied. // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.9 //

children.text: JaimGS 1.10:
children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 1.10:

children.text: athātaḥ prāśanakarma pūrvapakkṣe puṇye nakṣatre brāhmaṇānbhojayitvā haviṣyamannaṃ prāśayedannapate 'nnasya no dehyanamīvasya śuṣmiṇaḥ /
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>prāśanakarma</s> (first-feeding ceremony). In the waxing fortnight, on an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s>, having fed the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, he should feed [the child] sacrificial food, [reciting:] 'O lord of food (<s>Annapati</s>), give us food that is free from disease and full of vigor;

children.text: pra pradātāraṃ tāriṣa ūrjaṃ no dhehi dvipade śaṃ catuṣpada iti // JaimGS_1.10 //
children.translated_text: Promote the giver, bring him across; bestow nourishment upon us, well-being for the two-footed and the four-footed.' // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.10 //

children.text: JaimGS 1.11:
children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 1.11:

children.text: tṛtīye saṃvatsare jaṭāḥ kurvīta garbhatṛtīya ityeka udagayane pūrvapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre brāhmaṇānsvastivācyāparāhne 'gnaṃ praṇayitvā dakṣiṇato 'gneścatvāri pūrṇapātrāṇi nidadhyāhrīhiyavānāmabhito madhye tilamāṣāṇāmācāntodake 'nvārabdhe juhuyānmahāvyāhṛtibhirhutvā virūpākṣeṇātra pañcamīṃ juhoti sarvauṣadhibhi sphāṇṭamudakamānayanti vrīhiyavāstalamāṣā ityetatsarvauṣadhamāyamagātsavitā kṣureṇeti kṣuramādatta āyamagātsavitā kṣureṇa viśvairdevairanumato marudbhiḥ /

sa naḥ śivo bhavatu viśvakarmā yūyaṃ pāta svastibhiḥ sadā na ityuṣṇena vāya udakenehītyudakamādatta uṣṇena vāya udakenehyaditiḥ keśānvapatvityāpa undantu jīvasa iti dakṣiṇaṃ keśāntamabhyundyādāpa undantu jīvase dīrghāyuṣṭvāya varcasa iti tasmiṃstisro darbhapīñjūlīrupadadhātyekāṃ vā dhārayatu prajāpatiriti dhārayeddhārayatu prajāpatiḥ punaḥ punaḥ suvaptavā ityūrdhvaṃ trirādarśena spṛṣṭvā yena dhāteti kṣureṇa chindyādyena dhātā bṛhaspateragneridrasya cāyuṣe 'vapat /
children.translated_text: May he, <s>Viśvakarman</s>, be auspicious for us; do you all always protect us with blessings.' Thus — 'Come with warm water, O <s>Vāyu</s>' — he takes up the water — 'Come with warm water, O <s>Vāyu</s>; may <s>Aditi</s> shave the hair.' 'May the waters moisten for [your] living' — thus he should moisten the right side of the hair — 'May the waters moisten for living, for long life, for splendor.' Upon that he places three bunches of <s>darbha</s> grass, or one. 'May <s>Prajāpati</s> hold [it]' — thus he should hold — 'May <s>Prajāpati</s> hold [it] again and again; [the child] is to sleep well.' Having touched upward three times with a mirror — 'By which the Creator—' — with the razor he should cut — 'By which the Creator (<s>Dhātṛ</s>) shaved [the hair] for the long life of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, <s>Agni</s>, and <s>Indra</s>;

children.text: tena ta āyuṣe vapāmi suślokyāya svastaya iti yena tatprajāpatirmarudbhyo gṛhamedhibhyo 'vapat /
children.translated_text: With that I shave you for long life, for good fame, for well-being' — thus — 'By which <s>Prajāpati</s> shaved [the hair] for the <s>Maruts</s>, the householders;

children.text: tena ta āyuṣe vapāmi suślokyāya svastaya iti yena bhūyaścarātyayaṃ jyok ca paśyati sūryam /
children.translated_text: With that I shave you for long life, for good fame, for well-being' — thus — 'By which one walks about more and sees the sun for a long time.'

children.text: tena ta āyuṣe vapāmi suślokyāya svastya ityevaṃ paścāttathottarataḥ pratimantraṃ keśāṃśca darbhapiñjūlīśeṣāṃścānaḍuhe gomaye 'bhūmispṛṣṭe nidadhyāhbrahmaṇasya purastātpaścāditarayorvarṇayoryatkkṣureṇeti nāpitāya kṣuraṃ prayacchedyatkkṣureṇa mamlā vaptrā vapasi nāpitāṅgāni śuddhāni kurvāyurvarco mā hiṃsīrnāpiteti yathaiṣāṃ gotrakalpaḥ kulakalpo vāplute prāyaścittīrjuhuyādāvṛtaiva striyāḥ kuryādamantraṃ samantraṃ cetpaścajjuhuyādathāsya mūrdhānamārabhya japati triyāyuṣaṃ kaśyapasya jamadagnestriyāyuṣaṃ yaddevānāṃ triyāyuṣaṃ tatte astu triyāyuṣamiti dhānyapalvale goṣṭhe vā keśānnikhanetkuśalīkartā pūrṇapātrāṇi haredgaurdakkṣiṇā // JaimGS_1.11 //
children.translated_text: With that [razor], I shave you for long life, for good repute, for well-being — thus [reciting], behind [the head] and likewise on the north side, with each <s>mantra</s>. He should place the hair and the remaining <s>darbha</s>-grass tufts on a bull's cowdung not touching the ground. For a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, [shaving begins] from the front; for the other <s>varṇas</s>, from behind. Reciting 'yat kṣureṇa,' he should hand the razor to the barber: 'That you, O barber, shave with a razor, with a wet shaver — make the limbs clean; do not harm life or vigor, O barber.' According to their <s>gotra</s>-tradition or family-tradition. If [a mistake occurs while] not yet bathed, he should make <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiatory) offerings. For women, it should be done veiled, without <s>mantras</s>; if with <s>mantras</s>, he should offer afterwards. Then, touching his head, he recites: 'The triple lifespan of <s>Kaśyapa</s>, the triple lifespan of <s>Jamadagni</s>; that which is the triple lifespan of the gods — may that be your triple lifespan.' He should bury the hair in a grain-pond or cow-shed. The skilled one should receive full vessels. A cow is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.11 //

In the third year, one should perform the [tonsure of the] matted locks — some say 'in the third [year] from conception.' During the northern course of the sun (<s>udagayana</s>), in the waxing fortnight, on an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s>, having made <s>brāhmaṇas</s> pronounce benedictions, in the afternoon, having established the fire, he should place four full vessels to the south of the fire — of rice and barley on both sides, of sesame and <s>māṣa</s> beans in the middle. Having sipped water, when [the wife] has grasped [him from behind], he should offer oblations. Having offered with the <s>mahāvyāhṛtis</s>, he offers the fifth oblation with the <s>Virūpākṣa</s> verse. They bring warm water mixed with all herbs — rice, barley, sesame, and <s>māṣa</s> beans constitute 'all herbs.' '<s>Savitṛ</s> has come with the razor' — thus he takes up the razor — '<s>Savitṛ</s> has come with the razor, approved by all the gods and by the <s>Maruts</s>;

yathemaṃ jarimāṇa yājjyogrāṣṭre adhi jāgarājjīvāhi śaradaḥ śataṃ paśyāhi śaradaḥ śatamiti parīmaṃ poṣa brāhmaṇā mahe poṣāya dadhmasi /

yathemaṃ jarimāṇa yājjyok poṣe adhi jāgarājjīvāhi śaradaḥ śataṃ paśyāhi śaradaḥ śatamityathainaṃ paścādagneḥ prāṅbhukhamupaveśya yajñopavītinamācārya ācāmayatyācāntamutthāpyottarato 'gneḥ prāco darbhānāstīrya teṣvakṣatamaśmānamatyādhāya tatrainaṃ dakṣiṇena pādenāśmānam adhiṣṭhāpayedimamaśmānamārohāraśmeva tvaṃ sthiro bhava dviṣantamapabādhasva mā ca tvā dviṣato vadhīdityathainaṃ paścādagneḥ prāṅmukhamupaveśyottarata ācāryo 'nvārabdhe juhuyānmahāvyāhṛtibhirhutvā vedāhutibhiśca saṃpātamāsye bhūrṛcaḥ svāheti pratimantraṃ bhūrṛcaḥ svāhā bhuvo yajūṃṣi svāhā svaḥ sāmāni svāhaṃti prāśitamācāntamutthāpya namo vātāyetyenaṃ pradakṣiṇamagniṃ pariṇayennamo vātāya namo astvagnaye namaḥ pṛthivyai nama oṣadhībhyo namo vo 'dṛṣṭāya bṛhate karomītyadhigantaradhigaccha pradātaḥ prayacchāsāvamuṣmai vedamityathainaṃ paścādagneḥ prāṅmukhamavasthāpya purastādācāryaḥ pratyaṅmukhastāvajjalī kuruta uttarata ācāryastamanyo 'dbhiḥ pūrayennisrāveṇetarasya pūraṇamathainaṃ saṃśāsti brahmacaryamagāmupa mā nayasveti ko nāmāsītyasāviti nāmadheyaṃ dadyāttatrācāryo japati hiṃ bhūrbhuvaḥ svārāgantrā samaganmahi pra su martyaṃ yuyotana /
children.translated_text: live a hundred autumns, see a hundred autumns.' Then, seating him behind the fire facing east, wearing the <s>yajñopavīta</s> (sacred thread), the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) makes him sip water. Having raised him after sipping, having spread <s>darbha</s> grass north of the fire pointing eastward, having placed upon them an unbroken stone, he should make him stand on the stone with the right foot [reciting]: 'Ascend this stone; be firm like a rock; drive away the enemy; may the enemy not slay you.' Then, seating him behind the fire facing east, the <s>ācārya</s>, with [the student] having grasped [him], should offer with the <s>Mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great utterances) and with the <s>Veda</s>-offerings, [pouring] the remainder into his mouth — '<s>Bhūḥ</s>, the <s>Ṛcs</s>, <s>svāhā</s>' — with each <s>mantra</s>: '<s>Bhūḥ</s>, the <s>Ṛcs</s>, <s>svāhā</s>; <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, the <s>Yajus</s>-formulas, <s>svāhā</s>; <s>Svaḥ</s>, the <s>Sāmans</s>, <s>svāhā</s>.' Having raised him after eating and sipping, [reciting] 'Homage to <s>Vāyu</s>,' he should lead him around the fire clockwise: 'Homage to <s>Vāyu</s>, homage be to <s>Agni</s>, homage to the earth, homage to the herbs, homage to you, the unseen great one, I make [this obeisance].' 'O seeker, attain! O giver, grant! So-and-so gives the <s>Veda</s> to so-and-so.' Then, placing him behind the fire facing east, the <s>ācārya</s> standing in front facing west, they should both make the <s>añjali</s> gesture; from the north, the <s>ācārya</s>, and another person should fill [his hands] with water by pouring into the other's. Then he instructs him: 'I have entered <s>brahmacarya</s> (the vow of sacred studentship); initiate me.' 'What is your name?' 'I am so-and-so' — he should give his name. There the <s>ācārya</s> recites: '<s>hiṃ bhūḥ bhuvaḥ svaḥ</s>! We who have come together — extend mortal life!'

children.text: ariṣṭāḥ saṃcaremahi svasti caratādayamityathāsya dakṣiṇena hastena dakṣiṇaṃ hastaṃ gṛhṇātīndraste hastamagrabhīddhātā hastamagrabhītpūṣā hastamagrabhītsavitā hastamagrabhīryamā hastamagrabhīnmitrastvamasi dharmaṇāgnirācāryasteveti prāṇānāṃ granthirasīti nābhideśamārabhya japati prāṇānāṃ granthirasi mā visrasāmṛta mṛtyorantaraṃ kurviti dakṣiṇamaṃsamanvavamṛśya mayi vrate iti hṛdayaṃ te astu mama cittamanucittaṃ te astu /
children.translated_text: 'May we move about unharmed; may this one fare well.' Then with his right hand he grasps his right hand [reciting]: '<s>Indra</s> grasped your hand first, <s>Dhātṛ</s> grasped your hand, <s>Pūṣan</s> grasped your hand, <s>Savitṛ</s> grasped your hand, <s>Yama</s> grasped your hand; you are <s>Mitra</s> by law; <s>Agni</s> is your <s>ācārya</s> (teacher).' [Reciting] 'You are the knot of the vital breaths,' touching the navel region, he recites: 'You are the knot of the vital breaths; do not become loosened! O immortal one, create a space from death!' Touching the right shoulder: 'Be in my vow.' 'May your heart be [devoted to me]; may your mind follow my mind.'

children.text: mama vācamekavrato jupasva bṛhaspatistvā niyunaktu mayītyathainaṃ paridadātyagraye tvā paridadāmi vāyave tvā paridadāmi davāya tvā savitre paridadāmyadbhyastvauṣadhībhyaḥ paridadāmi sarvebhyastvā devebhyaḥ paridadāmi sarvebhyastvā bhūtebhyaḥ paridadāmyariṣṭyā ityathainaṃ saṃśāsti brahmacāryasi samidha ādhehyāpo 'śāna karma kuru mā divā svāpsīrityagnaye samidhamāhārṣamiti ghṛtenāktāḥ samidha ādadhātyagnaye samidhamāhārṣa bṛhate jātavedase /
children.translated_text: 'Delight in my speech with single devotion; may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> yoke you to me.' Then he entrusts him: 'I entrust you to <s>Agri</s>; I entrust you to <s>Vāyu</s>; I entrust you to <s>Savitṛ</s>; I entrust you to the waters and herbs; I entrust you to all the gods; I entrust you to all beings — for safety.' Then he instructs him: 'You are a <s>brahmacārin</s> (sacred student). Place fuel [on the fire]. Sip water. Do your work. Do not sleep by day.' [Reciting] 'I have brought fuel for <s>Agni</s>,' he places fuel-sticks anointed with <s>ghṛta</s> (clarified butter): 'I have brought fuel for <s>Agni</s>, for the great <s>Jātavedas</s>;

children.text: yathā tvamagne samidhā samidhyasa evamahamāyuṣā varcasā tejasā sanyā medhayā prajñayā prajayā paśubhirbrahmavarcasenānnādyena dhanena samedhichīya svāhā //
children.translated_text: just as you, O <s>Agni</s>, are kindled with fuel, so may I prosper with life, vigor, splendor, wealth, intelligence, wisdom, offspring, cattle, <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual splendor), food, and riches, <s>svāhā</s>!'

One should initiate (<s>upanayana</s>) a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> in the seventh year, in the fifth if one desires <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual splendor), but in the ninth if one desires long life; a <s>kṣatriya</s> in the eleventh, a <s>vaiśya</s> in the twelfth. One should not initiate beyond the sixteenth year, for he whose virility has developed becomes fallen [from his caste]. Then they bring him, bathed, adorned, with anointed eyes, and having had the barber's work done. He should clothe him with a new garment [reciting]: 'We place this [garment] around with the prayer of <s>Soma</s> and <s>Brahman</s> for hearing; so that this one may reach old age, may he ever be wakeful in hearing; live a hundred autumns, see a hundred autumns' — according to the <s>varṇa</s>. 'We place this around with the prayer of <s>Indra</s> and <s>Brahman</s> for sovereignty; so that this one may reach old age, may he ever be wakeful in sovereignty; live a hundred autumns, see a hundred autumns.' 'We place this around with the prayer of <s>Brahman</s> for prosperity; so that this one may reach old age, may he ever be wakeful in prosperity;

children.text: apsarāsu yā medhā gandharveṣu ca yanmanaḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever intelligence (<s>medhā</s>) is among the <s>Apsarases</s>, and whatever mind among the <s>Gandharvas</s> —

children.text: daivī medhā manuṣyajā sā māṃ medhā surabhirjuṣatāṃ svāhā //
children.translated_text: that divine intelligence, born among humans — may that fragrant intelligence delight in me, <s>svāhā</s>!'

sā mā samantādabhiryehi bhadre bhartāraste mekhale mā riṣāmeti mauñjīṃ brāhmaṇasya maurvīṃ rājanyasya muñjamiśrāṃ tāmalīṃ vaiśyasya mauñjīṃ vā sarveṣāmatha paridhanāni kṣaumaṃ vā śāṇaṃ vāntaraṃ brāhmaṇasyaiṇeyamuttaraṃ rauravaṃ rājanyasyājaṃ vaiśyasyaiṇeyaṃ vā sarveṣāṃ svastyayano 'sīti daṇḍaṃ prayacchetprāṇasaṃmitaṃ pālāśaṃ brāhmaṇasya bailvaṃ brahmavarcasakāmasya naiyagrodhaṃ rājanyasyaudumbaraṃ vaiśyasya pālāśaṃ vā sarveṣāṃ mātaraṃ prathamaṃ bhikṣetāthānyāḥ suhṛdo bhavatpūrvayā brāhmaṇo bhikṣeta bhavati bhikṣāṃ dehīti bhavanmadhyamayā rājanyo bhikṣāṃ bhavati dehīti bhavadantyavaiśyo dehi bhikṣāṃ bhavatīti kṣāṃ ca hiṃ ca na vardhayedbhavatpūrvayā vā sarve prāyaścittaṃ cedutpadyeta jīvā stha jīvayata metyenamapa ācāmayejjīvā stha jīvayata māpo nāma sthāmṛtā nāma stha svadhā nāma stha tāsāṃ vo bhukṣiṣīya sumatau mā dhatta śivā me bhavata namo vo 'stu mā mā hiṃsiṣṭeti bhaikṣamupanyāhṛtamūrdhvaṃ trirātrātsāvitrīṃ prabrūyāttadaharvā paścādagneḥ pacchor'dharcaśaḥ sarvāmityanūcya vedamārabhyāgne vratapata iti ghṛtenāktāḥ samidha ādadhātyagre vratapata vrataṃ cariṣyāmi tacchakeyaṃ tanme rādhyatāṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: 'Come to me from all sides, O auspicious one; may we, your wearers, O girdle, not be harmed.' A <s>mauñjī</s> (muñja-grass girdle) for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, a <s>maurvī</s> (bowstring) for a <s>rājanya</s> (kṣatriya), a <s>tāmalī</s> fiber mixed with <s>muñja</s> for a <s>vaiśya</s>, or <s>mauñjī</s> for all. The garments: linen or hemp as the inner garment for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, an antelope skin as the upper; a <s>ruru</s>-deer skin for a <s>rājanya</s>, a goat skin for a <s>vaiśya</s>, or antelope for all. [Reciting] 'You are the path to well-being,' he gives the staff — reaching up to the breath [i.e., the nose], of <s>palāśa</s> wood for a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, of <s>bilva</s> for one desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s>, of <s>nyagrodha</s> (banyan) for a <s>rājanya</s>, of <s>udumbara</s> (fig) for a <s>vaiśya</s>, or <s>palāśa</s> for all. He should beg [alms] from his mother first, then from other well-wishers. A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> begs with <s>bhavat</s> placed first: 'Lady, give alms.' A <s>rājanya</s> with <s>bhavat</s> in the middle: 'Alms, lady, give.' A <s>vaiśya</s> with <s>bhavat</s> at the end: 'Give alms, lady.' One should not alter 'kṣāṃ' or 'hiṃ' — or all may beg with <s>bhavat</s> first. If an expiation is required: 'You are alive, give me life' — thus he should make him sip water: 'You are alive, give me life! O waters, you are called by name; you are immortal by name; you are called <s>svadhā</s>; I wish to partake of you; place me in your goodwill; be auspicious to me; homage to you; do not harm me.' After the begged food has been presented, after three nights — or on that very day — he should recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [to him], behind the fire facing west, by half-verses and then in full. Having thus commenced the <s>Veda</s> study, [reciting] '<s>Agne</s>, lord of vows,' he places fuel-sticks anointed with <s>ghṛta</s>: 'O <s>Agni</s>, lord of vows, I shall observe the vow; may I be capable of it; may it be fulfilled for me, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: vāyo vratapate vrataṃ cariṣyāmi tacchakeyaṃ tanme sādhyatāṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Vāyu</s>, lord of vows, I shall observe the vow; may I be capable of it; may it be accomplished for me, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: āditya vratapate vrataṃ cariṣyāmi tacchakeyaṃ tanme rādhyatāṃ svāhā /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Āditya</s>, lord of vows, I shall observe the vow; may I be capable of it; may it be fulfilled for me, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: vratānāṃ vratapate vrataṃ cariṣyāmi tacchakeyaṃ tanme rādhyatāṃ svāheti tadetaddṛtādeśanaṃ sarvatra vratasamāptāvagre vratapate vratamacāriṣaṃ tadaśakaṃ tanme 'rādhi svāheti mantrānsaṃnamayedathainaṃ saṃśāsti brahmacāryācāryādhīnaḥ praśānto 'dhaḥśāyī daṇḍamekhalājinajaṭādhārī svyanṛtamadhumāṃsagandhamālyavarjī bhaveti trirātramakṣārālavaṇāśyūrdhvaṃ trirātrātprācīṃ vodīcīṃ vā diśamupaniṣkramya palāśaṃ gatvā vyāhṛtibhirabhyajya sthālīpākeneṣṭvā yajñopavītaṃ daṇḍamityudasya pratyeyādgaurdakṣiṇā // JaimGS_1.12 //
children.translated_text: 'O lord of vows among vows, I shall observe the vow; may I be capable of it; may it be fulfilled for me, <s>svāhā</s>!' This is the declaration of the cosmic order (<s>ṛtādeśana</s>), [applicable] everywhere. At the conclusion of every vow [one recites]: 'O <s>Agni</s>, lord of vows, I have observed the vow; I was capable of it; it has been fulfilled for me, <s>svāhā</s>.' He should recite the <s>mantras</s> in conjunction. Then he instructs him: 'A <s>brahmacārin</s> is subject to the <s>ācārya</s>, tranquil, sleeping on the ground, wearing the staff, girdle, skin, and matted locks, avoiding falsehood, honey, meat, perfume, and garlands.' For three nights, he should eat food without alkali or salt. After three nights, going out toward the eastern or northern direction to a <s>palāśa</s> tree, anointing [it] with the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s>, having sacrificed with <s>sthālīpāka</s> (cooked grain offering), discarding the <s>yajñopavīta</s> (sacred thread) and staff, he should return. A cow is the <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (sacrificial fee). // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.12 //

'<s>Bhūḥ svāhā</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ svāhā</s>, <s>Svaḥ svāhā</s>, <s>Bhūr Bhuvaḥ Svaḥ svāhā</s>.' [Reciting] 'iyaṃ duruktāt,' he ties the <s>mekhalā</s> (girdle): 'This one, warding off evil speech, purifying my complexion as a purifier, has come. Bringing strength through inhalation and exhalation, this girdle is a divine, blessed sister. Protector of cosmic order (<s>ṛta</s>), nourisher of austerity (<s>tapas</s>), destroying <s>rakṣas</s> (demons), overcoming foes.'

children.text: sāyaṃprātarudakānte pūto bhūtvā sapavitro 'jadbhirmārjayetāpohiṣṭhīyābhistisṛbhistaratsa mandī dhāvatīti catasṛbhirvāmadevyamante śucau deśe darbheṣvāsīno darbhāndhārayamāṇaḥ pratyaṅmukho vāgyataḥ sandhyāṃ manasā dhyāyedā nakṣatrāṇāmudayāduditeṣu nakṣatreṣu trīnprāṇāyāmāndhārayitvā sāvitrīṃ sahasrakṛtva āvartayecchatakṛtvo vā daśāvaramathāgnimupatiṣṭhate 'gne tvaṃ no antama ityatha varuṇamupatiṣṭhate tvaṃ varuṇa uta mitra ityetayaivāvṛtā prātaḥ prāṅmukhastiṣṭhannathādityamupatiṣṭhata udvayaṃ tamasasparītyatha mitramupatiṣṭhate pra mitrāya prāryamṇa iti sa yadi sūryābhyuditaḥ sūryābhinimukto vā taccheṣaṃ sāvitrīṃ manasā dhyāyetsaiva tatra prāyaścittiḥ // JaimGS_1.13 //
children.translated_text: At the evening and morning <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight worship), at the end of [touching] water, having become purified, wearing the <s>pavitra</s> (purifying ring of kuśa grass), one should cleanse oneself with water using the three [verses] beginning with '<s>Āpo hiṣṭhīyā</s>' and the four [verses] '<s>Taratsa mandī dhāvatī</s>,' and [reciting] the <s>Vāmadevya</s> <s>sāman</s>. Afterwards, seated on <s>darbha</s> grass in a pure place, holding <s>darbha</s> grass, facing west, observing silence, one should meditate on the <s>sandhyā</s> mentally until the rising of the stars. When the stars have risen, having held three <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath-controls), one should repeat the <s>Sāvitrī</s> a thousand times, or a hundred times, or at least ten times. Then one worships <s>Agni</s> with '<s>Agne tvaṃ no antama</s>' ('O <s>Agni</s>, you are nearest to us'). Then one worships <s>Varuṇa</s> with '<s>Tvaṃ Varuṇa uta Mitra</s>' ('You, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Mitra</s>'). In the same manner, in the morning, standing facing east, one worships <s>Āditya</s> with '<s>Ud vayaṃ tamasas parī</s>' ('We have risen above the darkness'). Then one worships <s>Mitra</s> with '<s>Pra Mitrāya prāryamṇa</s>' ('Forth to <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Aryaman</s>'). If the sun has risen before him or set before him, he should meditate on the remaining <s>Sāvitrī</s> mentally — that itself is the expiation (<s>prāyaścitta</s>) in that case. // JaimGS 1.13 //

children.translated_text: The <s>upākaraṇa</s> (commencement of Vedic study) is on the full moon of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, or on that of <s>Prauṣṭhapada</s>. With the hand, having performed three <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> and having sipped water (<s>ācamana</s>), all recite the preliminary recitation (<s>japa</s>) together: 'May we be together, may we eat together, may our vigor be together, let us not hate one another, may all our vigor be together.' He should declare the <s>Sāvitrī</s> to them as at the <s>upanayana</s> (initiation), and mentally the <s>Sāma-Sāvitrī</s> also. Having studied the <s>Chandas</s> (Vedic meters) beginning with '<s>Somaṃ rājānam</s>' ('King <s>Soma</s>'), as is proper, with unhusked grain and curds, one offers nine oblations: 'The <s>ṛṣis</s>, the <s>Chandas</s>, the <s>ṛcs</s>, the <s>yajus</s>-formulas, the <s>sāmans</s> — we worship <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s>, <s>Sadaspati</s> the wondrous, the giver of wisdom.' With the first six of these, one should first offer <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) to the teacher, and the [line of] teachers: <s>Jaimini</s>, <s>Talavakāra</s>, <s>Sātyamugra</s>, <s>Rāṇāyani</s>, <s>Durvāsas</s> and <s>Bhāguri</s>, <s>Gauruṇiḍa</s>, <s>Gorgulavi</s>, the venerable <s>Aupamanyava</s>, <s>Kāraḍi</s>, <s>Sāvarṇi</s>, <s>Gārgya</s>, <s>Vārṣagaṇya</s>, <s>Daivantya</s> — these thirteen. Having consecrated the oblation-remainder with the two [mantras] '<s>Dhānāvantaṃ</s>' and '<s>Dadhikrāvṇa</s>,' and having eaten the remainder of the offering, one studies in the forenoon. When the <s>Āgneya</s> (section on <s>Agni</s>) is completed, a goat [is the sacrificial fee]; for the <s>Aindra</s> (section on <s>Indra</s>), a ram; for the <s>Pāvamāna</s> (purificatory section), a cow is the <s>parva</s>-fee. One should feed fellow-students who have approached. The <s>Sāvitra</s> day [is observed]. Those desiring [merit] at the <s>utsarga</s> (conclusion of study) should not eat meat on the night of [full moon], nor perform <s>śrāddha</s>, nor cut hair, nor approach a woman — except one's wife during her season. [The period of study lasts] through the rainy and autumn seasons — some say half a month. // JaimGS 1.14 //

children.text: taiṣīmutsargo vedeṣu yathāsvaṃ viśramantāṃ chandāṃsi caturattarāṇi śivena no dhyāyantvityutsṛjyādhyāyanadhyāsau vratāni cānupālayanto yathāsvaṃ vedamadhīyīrannata ūrdhvamabhreṣu nādhīyate // JaimGS_1.15 //
children.translated_text: The <s>utsarga</s> (conclusion of Vedic study) is on the full moon of <s>Pauṣa</s> (month of <s>Taiṣa</s>). One suspends study in the <s>Vedas</s>, each according to his own, [saying]: 'May the <s>Chandas</s> (sacred meters) rest, being four and more; may they meditate upon us auspiciously' — thus releasing them. Observing the study-rules and vows, they should study each his own <s>Veda</s>. From that point onward, one does not study when there are clouds. // JaimGS 1.15 //

children.text: gaudānikavrātikaupaniṣadāḥ saṃvatsarāsteṣu sāyaṃprātarudakopasparśanaṃ nānupaspṛśya bhojanaṃ prātaḥ sāyamupaspṛśyā samidādhānādaraṇyātsamidhamāhṛtyādadhyādādityavrātikaḥ saṃvatsara ekavāsā na yuktamārohedādityaṃ nāntardadhīta chatreṇa mahīmāsanaśayānābhyāmupānadbhyāṃ ca nordhvaṃ jānvorapaḥ prasnāyādanyatrācāryavacanāhrātike vrataparvādityavrātike śukriyāṇyaupaniṣada upaniṣadaṃ śrāvayet // JaimGS_1.16 //
children.translated_text: The <s>Gaudānika</s>, <s>Vrātika</s>, and <s>Aupaniṣada</s> [observances] are year-long. In these, evening and morning water-touching (<s>upasparśana</s>) [is required]; one should not eat without having touched water. In the morning and evening, having touched water and having offered a fuel-stick (<s>samidh</s>), having brought the fuel-stick from the forest, one should add it [to the fire]. The <s>Ādityavrātika</s> [observance]: for one year, wearing a single garment, one should not mount a yoked [vehicle], should not hide the sun with an umbrella, should not [sit on] the ground with a seat or bed or sandals, and should not bathe above the knees in water, except by the teacher's instruction. In the <s>Vrātika</s> [observance], the <s>vrata-parva</s> rites [are performed]; in the <s>Ādityavrātika</s>, the <s>Śukriya</s> rites; in the <s>Aupaniṣada</s>, one should recite the <s>Upaniṣad</s>. // JaimGS 1.16 //

children.text: dvādaśa mahānāmnikāḥ saṃvatsarā nava ṣaṭ traya iti vikalpāḥ saṃvatsaramityeke pitrā cecchrutā mahānāmnyaḥ saṃvatsaraṃ brahmacaryaṃ carecchuklaikavāsā vrataṃ tu bhūyastiṣṭheddivāthāsīta naktaṃ tasya kṛṣṇe bhojanācchādane bhavata ityeke śuklaṃ caiva paridadhyādrāgadoṣānna kṛṣṇaṃ sarvāsvapsūpaspṛśedabuktāḥ śakvarya iti nāvā na prasnāyātprāṇasaṃśaye tūpaspṛśedubhayata api vā gāḥ pāyayetpaśuktāḥ śakvarya iti varṣaṃ nāntardadhīta chatreṇa prati varṣaṃ niṣkrāmedevamasya carataḥ kāmavarṣī parjanyo bhavati brahmacaryānta ekarātramupoṣita araṇyaṃ gatvā śaivalamiśrāṇāmapāṃ kāṃsaṃ pūrayitvā tamupaveśya samanuparigṛhya nimīlitaṃ tisra stotriyā upagāyetsapurīṣā upotthāyācāryo 'hatena vāsasā mukhamasya pariṇahyetpradakṣiṇamudapātraṃ dhārayaṃstiṣṭhedahaḥśeṣaṃ rātrimāsīta vāgyataḥ śvo bhate 'raṇyaṃ gatvāgnimupasamādhāya vatsamupānvānīye vāsa udveṣṭayedudyamya kāṃsamapo 'bhivīkṣa iti vīkṣetsvarabhivīkṣa ityādityaṃ jyotirabhivīkṣa ityagniṃ paśumabhivīkṣa iti vatsaṃ samanyā yantītyapaḥ prasicya vāsaḥ kāṃsaṃ vatsamityacāryāyopaharetsthālīpākādviśvāmitrendrau mahānāmnīśca yajata ityācāryaṃ sapariṣaṭkaṃ bhojayedgaurdakṣiṇā // JaimGS_1.17 //
children.translated_text: Twelve years are the <s>Mahānāmnī</s> observances — or nine, six, or three, as alternatives; one year, according to some. If the <s>Mahānāmnīs</s> have been heard from the father, one should observe celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>) for one year, wearing a single white garment. The <s>vrata</s> (observance) lasts longer: during the day one should sit; at night [one should lie on the ground]. In the dark [fortnight], food and clothing should be [dark] — so say some; but one should also wear white, since black is a fault due to passion. One should touch water at all [occasions]; having not eaten, [one recites] '<s>Śakvaryas</s>.' One should not bathe with a boat; but in danger to life, one may touch water on both sides. Or, one may water cows, [reciting] '<s>Paśuktāḥ Śakvarya</s>.' For one year, one should not hide the sun with an umbrella. Each year one should go forth [from the village]. Thus, for one who observes this, the rain-god <s>Parjanya</s> rains at will. At the end of the celibacy period, having fasted for one night, having gone to the forest and filled a bronze vessel with water mixed with moss (<s>śaivāla</s>), having seated him [the student] and embraced him all around with eyes closed, [the teacher] should chant three <s>stotriyas</s> (laudatory verses). Having arisen with excrement [vessels], the teacher should bind his face with an unworn garment. Holding the water-vessel to the right, he should stand for the remainder of the day; at night he should sit, observing silence. The next morning, having gone to the forest and having built the fire, having brought a calf near, one should unwrap the garment; raising the bronze vessel, one should gaze at the water [saying] '<s>Apo abhivīkṣa</s>' ('Gaze at the waters'), gaze at the sun [saying] '<s>Svar abhivīkṣa</s>' ('Gaze at the light'), gaze at the fire [saying] '<s>Jyotir abhivīkṣa</s>' ('Gaze at the radiance'), gaze at the calf [saying] '<s>Paśum abhivīkṣa</s>' ('Gaze at the animal'). [Reciting] '<s>Sam anyā yantī</s>' ('They flow together'), having poured out the water, one should present the garment, the bronze vessel, and the calf to the teacher. From a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (cooked offering), one offers to <s>Viśvāmitra</s> and <s>Indra</s> and the <s>Mahānāmnīs</s> with 'We worship.' One should feed the teacher together with his retinue. A cow is the fee. // JaimGS 1.17 //

children.translated_text: JaimGS 1.18:

children.text: dvādaśa varṣāṇi vedabrahmacaryaṃ jananātprabhṛtītyeke yāvadadhyayanaṃ vā sadā sāye samidādhānaṃ sāyaṃprātarbhaikṣacaraṇaṃ dve trivṛtī varjayetrivṛtaṃ ca maṇiṃ triguṇe copānahau ṣoḍaśe godānakaraṇaṃ tatkeśāntakaraṇamityācakṣate cauḍakaraṇena mantrā vyākhyātā upanayanena vratādeśanaṃ na tviha niyuktamahataṃ vāsaḥ sarvāṇi lomanakhāni vāpayecchikhāvarjamityaudgāhamaniruptakeśaḥ snāyādvanaspateriti vanaspatīnāṃ snānīyena tvacamunmṛdgīte vanaspatestvagasi śodhani śodhaya mā tāṃ tvābhiharaṃ dīrghāyuṣṭvā varcasa iti vanaspatīnāṃ gandho 'sīti snātvānulepanena kurute vanaspatīnāṃ gandho 'si puṇyagandha puṇyaṃ me gandhaṃ kuru devamanuṣyeṣu taṃ tvābhihare dīrghāyuṣṭvāya varcasa iti vanaspatīnāṃ puṣpamasīti srajamābadhnīte vanaspatīnāṃ puṣpamasi puṇyagandha puṇyaṃ me gandhaṃ kuru devamanuṣyeṣu taṃ tvābhihare dīrghāyuṣṭvāya varcasa ityādarśo 'sītyādarśa ātmānaṃ vīkṣetādarśo 'syā mā dṛśyāsandevamanuṣyā ubhaye śobho 'si śobhāsamahaṃ devamanuṣyeṣu roco 'si rocāsamahaṃ devamanuṣyeṣvityapoddhṛtya srajamādeśayetoktā dharmāḥ saṃvatsareṣu gaurdakṣiṇā // JaimGS_1.18 //
children.translated_text: Twelve years is the Vedic celibacy (<s>vedabrahmacaryam</s>) — from birth, according to some; or for as long as the study [continues]. Always at evening, the offering of fuel-sticks; evening and morning, the round of begging for food. Two triple-twisted [cords] should be avoided, as well as a triple-twisted girdle and triple-strung sandals. In the sixteenth [year], the <s>godāna</s> (hair-offering) ceremony is performed — they call that the <s>keśānta</s> (hair-cutting) rite. The <s>mantras</s> are explained by the <s>cauḍakaraṇa</s> (tonsure ceremony); the instruction of vows by the <s>upanayana</s>; but here the binding is not for the great ones. One should shave all body hair and nails, except the topknot (<s>śikhā</s>) — thus says <s>Audgāhāmani</s>. With loosened hair, one should bathe [reciting] '<s>Vanaspateḥ</s>' ('Of the forest lord'), with the bark of forest trees as bathing material; one should rub the skin [reciting] '<s>Vanaspates tvag asi śodhani śodhaya mā, tāṃ tvābhiharaṃ dīrghāyuṣṭvā varcasa</s>' ('O forest lord, you are the purifying bark; purify me; I bring you for long life and luster'). After bathing, one applies ointment [reciting] '<s>Vanaspatīnāṃ gandho 'si puṇyagandha, puṇyaṃ me gandhaṃ kuru devamanuṣyeṣu, taṃ tvābhihare dīrghāyuṣṭvāya varcasa</s>' ('You are the fragrance of forest trees, O holy fragrance; make my fragrance holy among gods and humans; I bring you for long life and luster'). One ties on a garland [reciting] '<s>Vanaspatīnāṃ puṣpam asi puṇyagandha, puṇyaṃ me gandhaṃ kuru devamanuṣyeṣu, taṃ tvābhihare dīrghāyuṣṭvāya varcasa</s>' ('You are the flower of forest trees, O holy fragrance; make my fragrance holy among gods and humans; I bring you for long life and luster'). One looks at oneself in a mirror [reciting] '<s>Ādarśo 'si, ā mā dṛśyāsan devamanuṣyā ubhaye, śobho 'si, śobhā sam ahaṃ devamanuṣyeṣu, roco 'si, rocāsam ahaṃ devamanuṣyeṣu</s>' ('You are a mirror; may both gods and humans see me; you are beauty, may I be beautiful among gods and humans; you are radiance, may I be radiant among gods and humans'). Having removed [the previous garland], one should designate a [new] garland. The prescribed rites during the [study] years are as stated. A cow is the fee. // JaimGS 1.18 //
