children.translated_text: Having studied the <s>Veda</s> and having observed the vows, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> about to perform the <s>snāna</s> (bathing ceremony) prepares the requisite items: a new garment, <s>erakā</s> (reed-grass), bathing ointment, <s>sumanas</s> (jasmine) flowers, eye-ointment, a mirror, two new garments, a triple-stranded jewel, a bamboo staff, white sandals, and a barber equipped [with instruments]. He stands to the north. Having spread <s>erakā</s> grass and covered [him] with a new garment with its fringe turned upward, one seats him there facing east. One should cause the staff to sink in water, [saying] 'You are the thunderbolt against those who hate us!' One should loosen the girdle, [saying] 'Rise upward!' — and cause it also to sink in water. The <s>mantras</s> are explained by the <s>keśānta</s> (hair-cutting) ceremony, and the shaving: one shaves the head first, then the beard, then the other limbs in order — hair, beard, body-hair, and nails — and buries them at the root of an <s>aśvattha</s> or <s>udumbara</s> tree, [saying] 'My evil is struck away.' With cold and warm waters in which gold has been placed, one bathes him, [saying] 'O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, be auspicious, most benevolent, gentle to us; may your expanse not be visible.' One should bathe under <s>Rohiṇī</s> [nakṣatra, saying] 'This is the <s>nakṣatra</s> of <s>Prajāpati</s>; may I become rich in offspring!' — under <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, [saying] 'This is the <s>nakṣatra</s> of <s>Soma</s>; may the <s>Soma</s>-sacrifice not cease for me!' — under <s>Tiṣya</s>, [saying] 'This is the <s>nakṣatra</s> of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; <s>Brahman</s> is <s>Bṛhaspati</s>; may I become endowed with <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual radiance)!' — under <s>Hasta</s>, [saying] 'This is the <s>nakṣatra</s> of <s>Savitṛ</s>; may I be impelled by <s>Savitṛ</s>!' — under <s>Anūrādhā</s>, [saying] 'This is the <s>nakṣatra</s> of <s>Mitra</s>; may I be dear to friends!' — under <s>Śravaṇa</s>, [saying] 'This is the <s>nakṣatra</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; sacrifice indeed is <s>Viṣṇu</s>; may the sacrifice not cease for me!' One should dress him in a new garment, [saying] 'Protect this one, O <s>Soma</s>!' One should first anoint the left eye, [saying] 'With glory!' — then the right. One fastens the triple-stranded jewel on the neck. [One takes a staff] of <s>palāśa</s> if desiring well-being, [saying] 'You are the bringer of well-being'; of <s>bilva</s> if desiring <s>brahmavarcas</s>, [saying] 'May I become endowed with <s>brahmavarcas</s>!'; of <s>arka</s> if desiring food, [saying] 'May I become an eater of food!' [Saying] 'You are the <s>gandharva</s> <s>Viśvāvasu</s>; protect me, guard me!' — one takes the bamboo staff. One puts on the sandals, [saying] 'You are two guides; lead me!' — putting on the right one first. His vows are as follows: he should not seek to ridicule a woman whose body hair has not yet grown; he should not run when it rains; he should not carry sandals himself; he should not pick fruits himself; he should not go to another village toward evening; not alone; not with <s>śūdras</s>; he should not look into a water source; he should not climb a tree; he should not cross a narrow bridge; he should not sit in a concealed place; he should not eat food brought in through another door; not soured food; not twice-cooked; not stale — except vegetables, meat, barley-flour food, flattened rice, molasses, curds, honey, and ghee; he should not laugh without a proper jest; he should not bathe naked; he should not speak frivolous words; he should avoid gossip and quarrels. 'Three types of <s>snātakas</s> there are,' said <s>Āruṇi Gautama</s>: 'the knowledge-<s>snātaka</s>, the vow-<s>snātaka</s>, and the knowledge-and-vow-<s>snātaka</s>' — of these, the last is the best; the first two are equal. Having bathed, one should say to the teacher: 'Let the honored one bring me the <s>madhuparka</s> (honey-drink)!' — or one of teacher-like standing. To him, seated facing east, one brings the <s>madhuparka</s>: a seat, foot-water, <s>arghya</s> (respectful offering water), and mouth-rinsing water — one by one in order. He sits on the seat, washes the feet with the foot-water, [saying] 'May <s>Śrī</s> (prosperity) rest in me!' — the left foot first. If a <s>śūdrā</s> [woman washes his feet, he says] 'May splendor be in me!' — then the right. He accepts the <s>arghya</s> [saying] 'May radiance be in me!' and rinses the mouth with the rinsing water. On the pot-vessel placed on a seat, below are two seats placed with their tips touching, a single seat to the north; between them, curds and honey are placed together. If [mixed] with curds, it is a 'curd-mixture'; with water, a 'water-mixture'; with milk, a 'milk-mixture.' He accepts it [saying] 'Of the god, for you...' Having accepted it, having placed it on the ground, having controlled it, with the thumb and the little finger [he recites]: 'For myself, for you — for fame, for prosperity, for food, and for <s>brahmavarcas</s> (spiritual radiance)!' He eats three times; the remainder, having taken it northward, he gives to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, or having consecrated it, buries it in a pit for the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>. Then, another [attendant] stands with an axe in hand. Seeing the cow, he says 'Cow! Cow!' He addresses it with the verse: 'The cow is a milch-cow...' [saying] 'Release it!' — one should say. If it is to be slaughtered, one says 'Do it!' The cow's fat is to be offered.

children.text: mātā rudrāṇāṃ duhitā vasūnāṃ svasādityānāmamṛtasya nābhiḥ /
children.translated_text: She is the mother of the <s>Rudras</s>, the daughter of the <s>Vasus</s>, the sister of the <s>Ādityas</s>, the navel of immortality.

children.text: pra nu vocaṃ cikituṣe janāya mā gāmanāgāmaditiṃ vadhiṣṭa pibatūdakaṃ tṛṇānyattvityatha ṣaḍardhyārhā bhavantyṛtvigācāryaḥ snātako rājābhiṣiktaḥ priyaḥ sakhā śrotriyaśceti tebhya ātithyaṃ gāṃ kuryāttāmatithaya iti prokṣet // JaimGS_1.19 //
children.translated_text: I shall now speak to the discerning man: do not slay the cow — she who is sinless, she who is <s>Aditi</s>! Let her drink water and eat grass! Now, six are worthy of <s>arghya</s> (honorable reception): the <s>ṛtvik</s> (priest), the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher), a <s>snātaka</s>, a consecrated king, a dear friend, and a <s>śrotriya</s> (learned brāhmaṇa). For them, one should prepare a cow as guest-offering. One should sprinkle it [saying] 'For the guest.' // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.19 //

children.text: JaimGS 1.20:
children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 1.20:

children.text:
snātvā mātāpitarau paricarettadadhīnaḥ syāttābhyāmanujñāto jāyāṃ vindetānagnikāṃ samānajātīyāmasagotrāṃ māturasapiṇḍāṃ jyāyasaḥ kanīyasīṃ dūtamanumantrayate 'nṛkṣarā ṛjavaḥ santu panthā ebhiḥ sakhāyo yanti no vareyam /
samaryamā saṃ bhago no 'nunīyātsaṃ jāspatyaṃ suyamamastu devā iti pāṇigrahaṇe 'gnimāhriyamāṇamanumantrayate 'gniraitu prathamo devatānāṃ so 'syai prajāṃ muñcatu mṛtyupāśāt /
tadayaṃ rājā varuṇo 'numanyatāṃ yatheyaṃ strī pautramaghaṃ na rodāditi prajvalitamupatiṣṭhata imāmagnistrāyatāṃ gārhapatyaḥ prajāmasyai nayatu dīrghamāyuḥ /
children.translated_text: 'May king <s>Varuṇa</s> give consent to this, that this woman may not weep for her grandson's misfortune.' Thus one attends to the blazing [fire, saying]: 'May this <s>Gārhapatya</s> (household) fire protect her; may it lead her offspring to long life;'

children.text: aśūnyopasthā jīvatāmastu mātā pautramānandamabhi prabudhyatāmiyamiti purastādagrerbrāhmaṇo vāgyataḥ pratyaṅmukha udakumbhaṃ dhārayaṃstiṣṭheddakṣiṇato 'gneḥ śamīpalāśamiśrānlājāñchūrpe mātā dhārayenmāturabhāve tanmātrī pratyagagnererakāṃ tejanīṃ vānyadvaivaṃjātīyaṃ saṃveṣṭya nidadhyādyathā prasāryamāṇaṃ paścārdhaṃ barhiṣaḥ prāpnotyathāsyai vāsasī prokṣyānumanvya dadāti yā akṛntannavayanyā atanvata yāśca devīrantāmabhito 'dadanta /
children.translated_text: 'May this [woman] whose lap is never empty be a mother of living [children]; may she awaken to the joy of grandchildren.' Thus, before the fire, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, observing silence, facing westward, should stand holding a water-pot. To the south of the fire, the mother should hold in a winnowing basket parched grains mixed with <s>śamī</s> and <s>palāśa</s> [leaves]; in the absence of the mother, one having the standing of a mother. To the west of the fire, an <s>erakā</s> reed or <s>tejanī</s> stick or anything of that sort, having rolled it up, one should place it so that when unrolled it reaches the western half of the sacrificial grass. Then, having sprinkled and consecrated the two garments, one gives them to her [with the verse]: 'Those [women] who cut, those who wove, and those divine women who gave the ends [of the thread] —'

children.text: tāstvā devīrjarasā saṃvyayantvāyuṣmatīdaṃ paridhatsva vāsa iti tāṃ brūyādimāmerakāṃ dakṣiṇena pādenābhijahīti pra me patiyānaḥ panthāḥ kalpatāmityajapatyāṃ svayaṃ japetprāsyā iti dakṣiṇata erakāyāṃ bhāryāmupaveśyottarataḥ patirubhāvanvārabheyātāṃ svayamuccairjuhuyāñjāyāyāmanvārabdhāyāṃ mahāvyāhṛtibhirhutvā yā tiraścīti saptabhirjuhoti saṃpātaṃ prathamayā mūrdhanyāsiñcedyā tiraścī nipadyase 'haṃ vidharaṇī iti /
children.translated_text: 'May those divine [women] clothe you till old age; long-lived, put on this garment!' One should tell her: 'Strike this <s>erakā</s> reed with the right foot!' [She says:] 'May the path of my going to my husband be prepared!' Where she does not recite, he himself recites for her. Having seated the wife to the south of the <s>erakā</s>, the husband to the north, both should touch [the offering materials]. He himself should offer aloud, with the wife touching [the offerings]. Having offered with the <s>Mahāvyāhṛtis</s>, one offers with the seven [verses beginning] '<s>Yā tiraścī</s>.' With the first verse, one should pour the remainder on her head: 'You who lie crosswise, I am the supporter —'

children.text: tāṃ tvā dhṛtasya dhārayā saṃrādhā rādhayāmasi saṃrādhāyai svāhā //
children.translated_text: 'You, through the support of what is held, we gladden by fulfillment; for fulfillment, <s>svāhā</s>!'

Having bathed, one should attend to one's parents; one should be subject to them. With their permission, one should seek a wife — one who has not been previously married, of the same class, of a different <s>gotra</s>, not <s>sapiṇḍa</s> (related) to the mother, younger than the eldest [brother's wife]. One sends forth the messenger with [the verse]: 'May the paths be free from thorns and straight, on which our friends go to seek the bride; may <s>Aryaman</s> and <s>Bhaga</s> guide us together; may the married state be well-governed, O gods!' At the <s>pāṇigrahaṇa</s> (marriage hand-grasping ceremony), one accompanies the fire being brought with [the verse]: 'May <s>Agni</s> come first among the deities; may he release her offspring from the noose of death;'

children.text: mā te gṛhe niśi ghoṣa utthādanyatra tvadrudatyaḥ saṃviśantu /
children.translated_text: 'May no clamor arise in your house at night; may the weeping women lie down elsewhere than with you;'

children.text: mā tvaṃ vikeśyura āvadhiṣṭhā jīvapatnī patiloke virāja prajāṃ paśyantī sumanasyamānā svāhā /
children.translated_text: 'Do not stand upon [the pyre] with disheveled hair; as a living wife, shine in the world of your husband, beholding offspring and rejoicing, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: anvadya no 'numatiryajñaṃ deveṣu manyatām /
children.translated_text: 'May <s>Anumati</s> today approve our sacrifice among the gods;'

children.text: agniśca havyavāhanastatkarotu samṛdhyatāṃ svāhā //
children.translated_text: 'and may <s>Agni</s> the oblation-bearer accomplish that; may it prosper, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: dyauste pṛṣṭhaṃ rakṣatu vāyurūrū aśvinau ca stanaṃ dhayataste putrānsavitābhirakṣantu /
children.translated_text: 'May <s>Dyaus</s> protect your back, <s>Vāyu</s> your thighs, and the <s>Aśvins</s> your breasts; may <s>Savitṛ</s> guard your suckling sons;'

children.text: ā vāsasaḥ paridhānādbṛhaspatirviśve devā abhirakṣantu paścātsvāhā //
children.translated_text: 'From the putting on of garments, may <s>Bṛhaspati</s> and the <s>Viśvedevas</s> guard [her] from behind, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: aprajastāṃ pautramṛtyuṃ pāpmānamuta vādham /
children.translated_text: 'Childlessness, the death of grandsons, evil, and also affliction —'

children.text: śīrṣṇaḥ srajamivonmucya dviṣadbhya pratimuñcāmi pāśaṃ svāhā //
children.translated_text: 'casting off [these] like a wreath from the head, I fasten a noose upon the enemies, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: yāni kāni ca pāpāni sarvāṅgeṣu tavābhavan /
children.translated_text: 'Whatever evil deeds were upon all your limbs —'

children.text: pūrṇāhutibhirājyasya sarvāṇi tānyaśīśamaṃ svāhā //
children.translated_text: 'by full oblations of ghee, I have completely extinguished all of them, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: prajāpata ityekā // JaimGS_1.20 //
children.translated_text: 'To <s>Prajāpati</s>...' — this is one [additional oblation]. // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.20 //

children.text: JaimGS 1.21:
children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 1.21:

children.text: athāsyā dakṣiṇena pāṇinā dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ gṛhṇāti prahastaṃ puṃsa aṅgulī striyaḥ sāṅguṣṭhaṃ mithunakāmo gṛhṇāmi te saubhagatvāya hastaṃ mayā patyā jaradaṣṭiryathāsat /
children.translated_text: Then with his right hand he grasps her right hand — the outstretched hand; the fingers [if desiring] a male [child], [the palm if desiring] a female, with the thumb [included if] desiring both — [saying]: 'I grasp your hand for good fortune, that with me as your husband you may attain old age;'

children.text: bhago 'yemā savitā purandhirmahyaṃ tvādurgārhapatyāya devāḥ //
children.translated_text: '<s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Purandhī</s> — the gods have given you to me for householdership.'

children.text: somo 'dadadgandharvāya gandharvo 'dadagnaye /
children.translated_text: '<s>Soma</s> gave [her] to <s>Gandharva</s>, <s>Gandharva</s> gave [her] to <s>Agni</s>;'

children.text: rayiṃ ca putrāṃścādādagnirmahyamatho imām //
children.translated_text: 'and <s>Agni</s> gave me wealth and sons, and now this [bride].'

children.text: somaḥ prathamo vivide gandharvo vivida uttaraḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Soma</s> first obtained [her], <s>Gandharva</s> obtained [her] next;'

children.text: tṛtīyo 'gniṣṭe patisturīyo 'haṃ manuṣyajā ityupanayanāvṛtāśmānamadhiṣṭhāpayetsrīvat uttarapurastādagnerbhāryayā saṃprekṣyamāṇo japatyaghoracakṣurapatighnī ma edhi śivā patibhyaḥ sumanāḥ suvarcāḥ /
children.translated_text: '<s>Agni</s> is your third husband, I, born of men, am the fourth.' Thus, having led [her] around [the fire], he causes [her] to step upon a stone. To the northeast of the fire, looking at his wife, he recites: 'Be to me not of fierce gaze, not husband-slaying; be auspicious to [your] husband, of cheerful mind and radiance;'

children.text: jīvasūrdevakāmā syonā śaṃ no bhava dvipade śaṃ catuṣpade //
children.translated_text: 'Living, Sun-seeing, desiring the gods, be comfortable; be auspicious for us for bipeds, auspicious for quadrupeds!'

children.text: ā naḥ prajāṃ janayatu prajāpatirājarasāya samanatkaryamā /
children.translated_text: 'May <s>Prajāpati</s> beget offspring for us; may <s>Aryaman</s> unite [us] for old age;

children.text: adurmaṅgalīḥ patilokamāviśa śaṃ na edhi dvipade śaṃ catuṣpade //
children.translated_text: free from ill omen, enter the world of your husband; be auspicious for us for bipeds, auspicious for quadrupeds!'

children.text: tāṃ pūṣañchivatamāmerayasva yasyāṃ bījaṃ manuṣyā vapanti /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Pūṣan</s>, send her forth, the most auspicious one, in whom men sow the seed,

children.text: yā na ūrū uśatī vistrayātai yasyāmuśantaḥ praharema śepham //
children.translated_text: who willingly spreads her thighs for us, into whom, desirous, we may thrust the male organ.'

children.text: amo 'hamasmi sā tvaṃ sāmāhamasmyṛtkaṃ mano 'hamasmi vāktvaṃ dyaurahaṃ pṛthivī tvaṃ tāvehi saṃbhavāva saha reto dadhāvahai puṃse putrāya vettavai māmanuvratā bhava sadṛśayyā mayā bhavāsāvityathāsyā nāma gṛhītvāgniṃ parikrameyātāmīrtvamasyūkte mātā nāma sā māmehi saha prajayā saha rāyaspopeṇeti tasyāṃ pratyāvrajitāyāṃ bhrātānyo vā sūhṛdabhidhāritānlājāñchūrpādañjalinopaghātamañjalāvāvapedupastīrṇābhidhāritānkṛtvā tānitarāgnau juhuyātkanyaleyaṃ nāryaryamṇamiti kanyalā pitṛbhyaḥ patilokaṃ yatīyamava dīkṣāmayakṣata svāhā //
children.translated_text: 'I am he (<s>ama</s>), you are she (<s>sā</s>); I am the <s>Sāman</s>, you are the <s>Ṛc</s>; I am the mind, you are speech; I am heaven, you are earth — come, let us unite, let us deposit seed together, for a male child, for [our] benefit.' 'Be devoted to me; share a bed with me' — [then] having taken her name, he says: 'Come, let us circumambulate the fire — you are <s>Ūktā</s>, whose name is Mother; come to me together with offspring, together with wealth and prosperity.' When she has returned [from the circumambulation], a brother or another well-wisher, having held out parched grains (<s>lāja</s>) in a winnowing basket, pours them by the handful into [the bride's] cupped hands, placed on a layer of [grass]; having laid them on a substrate and held them forth, she offers them into the fire [with the mantra]: 'This maiden [offers] to <s>Aryaman</s>' — 'This maiden, departing to her husband's world from the <s>pitṛs</s> (ancestors), has relinquished the <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation), <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: iyaṃ nāryupabrūte 'gnau lājānāvapantī /
children.translated_text: 'This woman announces, casting the parched grains into the fire:,

children.text: dīrghāyurastu me patiredhantāṃ jñātayo mama svāhā //
children.translated_text: "May my husband be long-lived; may my kinsmen prosper, <s>svāhā</s>!"'

children.text:
aryamṇaṃ nu devaṃ kanyāgnimayakṣata /
sa imāṃ devo aryamā preto muñcātu māmutaḥ svāheti homānteṣu japati caturviśvā uta tvayā vayaṃ dhārā udanyā iva /
atigāhemahi dviṣa iti tūṣṇīṃ dhārikā kāmāyāvapeccaturthaṃ dakṣiṇaṃ śūrpapuṭaṃ kāma ityācakṣata uttarapurastādagraneḥ sapta padānyabhyutkramayedekamiṣa iti pratimantramekamiṣe viṣṇustvānvetu /
dve ūrje viṣṇustvānvetu /
trīṇi rāyaspoṣāya viṣṇustvānvetu /
catvāri mayobhavāya viṣṇustānvetu /
children.translated_text: Four steps for well-being — may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you!

children.text: ṣaḍṛtubhyo viṣṇustānvetu /
children.translated_text: Six steps for the seasons — may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you!

children.text: sakhā saptapadī bhaveti saptame prācīmavasthāpyodakumbhena mārjayerannāpohiṣṭhīyābhistisṛbhiḥ prekṣakānanumantrayate sumaṅgalīriyaṃ vadhūrimāṃ sameta paśyata /
children.translated_text: With the seventh [step], become a friend (<s>sakhā saptapadī bhava</s>)!' At the seventh step, having stationed [the bride] facing east, one anoints her with a water-pot, using the three verses of the <s>Āpohiṣṭhīya</s> [hymn]. One addresses the onlookers: 'This bride is auspicious; come together and behold her;

children.text: saubhāgyamasyai dattvāyāthāstaṃ viparetaneti prekṣayeddhruvamarundhatīṃ sapta ṛṣīnpaśyānīti pratijānānāṃ dhruvo 'sīti dhruvamupatiṣṭhate dhruvo 'si dhruvāhaṃ patikule bhūyāsamamuṣyeti patināma gṛhṇīyādasāvityātmano 'rundhatīmarundhatyaruddhāhaṃ patyā bhūyāsamamuneti patināma gṛhṇīyādasāvityātmanaḥ // JaimGS_1.21 //
children.translated_text: having given her good fortune, depart hence.' One makes her look at <s>Dhruva</s> (the Pole Star), <s>Arundhatī</s>, and the Seven Sages (<s>Saptarṣi</s>). As she declares 'Let me see [them],' she approaches <s>Dhruva</s> [saying]: 'You are firm; may I, [named] so-and-so, be firm in my husband's family' — taking the husband's name and her own. [Seeing] <s>Arundhatī</s> [she says]: '<s>Arundhatī</s>, [I am] <s>Arundhatī</s>; may I, unobstructed, be [united] with my husband, [named] so-and-so' — taking the husband's name and her own. // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.21 //

'She has worshipped the god <s>Aryaman</s>, the divine [patron of] maidens, through the fire; may this god <s>Aryaman</s> release her from here [from her father's family], not from that one [from her husband], <s>svāhā</s>!' At the end of each oblation, one recites: 'May we, together with you, like streams seeking water, overcome all hostility.' She silently casts in a fourth handful [of parched grains], holding the winnowing basket to the south — they call it '<s>kāma</s>' (desire). To the northeast of the fire, one makes her step forward seven steps [each with a mantra]: 'One step for nourishment — may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you! Two steps for vigor — may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you! Three steps for the increase of wealth — may <s>Viṣṇu</s> follow you!

children.text: JaimGS 1.22:
children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 1.22:

children.text:
pūṣā tveta iti prasthitāmanumantrayate pūṣā tveto nayatu hastagṛhyāśvinau tvā pravahatāṃ rathena /
gṛhāngaccha gṛhapatnī yathāso vaśinī tvaṃ vidathamāvadāsīti svaṃ kulaṃ prāptāṃ kalyāṇaśīlāḥ kalyāṇaprajāḥ samavajīrṇāḥ pratyavaropayantīha priyaṃ prajayā te samṛdhyatāmasmingṛhe gārhapatyāya jāgṛhi /
enā patyā tanvaṃ saṃsṛjasvāthājīvrī vidathamāvadāsīti pratyavaropyānaḍuhe carmaṇyuttaralomanyupaveśayediha gāvo niṣīdantvihāśvā iṅa puruṣāḥ /
iho sahasradakṣiṇo 'bhi pūṣā niṣīdatviti kumāramupastha ādhāya śakaloṭānāvapetphalāni yotthāpya kumāramanvārabdhāyāṃ juhuyādiha dhṛtirityaṣṭābhiḥ svāhākārāntairiha dhṛtiriha svadhṛtiriha rantiriha ramasva /
mayi dhṛtirmayi svadhṛtirmayi ramo mayi ramasveti trirātramakṣārālavaṇāśinau brahmacāriṇāvadhaḥ saṃveśināvasaṃvartamānau saha śayātāmūrdhvaṃ trirātrātsaṃbhavo niśāyāṃ jāyāpatikarmaṇyaṃ prāyaścittīrjuhuyādagre prāyaścitte tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittirasi brāhmaṇastvā nāthakāma upadhāvāmi yāsyai prajāghnī tanūstāmasyā apajahi svāhā /
vāyo prāyaścitte tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittirasi brāhmaṇastvā nāthakāma upadhāvāmi yāsyai paśughnī tanūstāmasyā apajahi svāhā /
sūrya prayaścitte tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittirasi brāhmaṇastvā nāthakāma upadhāvāmi yāsyai patighni tanūstāmasyā apajahi svāhā /
children.translated_text: 'You are the <s>prāyaścitta</s> of the gods, O <s>Sūrya</s>. I, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, seek your protection. Whatever form of hers destroys the husband — remove that from her, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: candra prāyaścitte tvaṃ devānāṃ prāyāścittarasi brahmaṇastvā nāthakāma upadhāvāmi yāsyai gṛhaghni tanūstāmasyā apajahi svāhā /
children.translated_text: 'You are the <s>prāyaścitta</s> of the gods, O <s>Candra</s> (Moon). I, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, seek your protection. Whatever form of hers destroys the household — remove that from her, <s>svāhā</s>!'

children.text: agne vāyo sūrya candra prāyaścittayo yūyaṃ devānāṃ prāyaścittaya stha brāhmaṇo vo nāthakāma upadhāvāmi yāsyai yaśoghnītanūstāmasyā apahata svāheti sthālīpākādagniṃ prajāpatiṃ ceṣṭvā saṃpātāṃścamasa ānīya srotāṃsyāṅkṣvetyenāṃ brūyānnābhiṃ prathamaṃ tato yānyūrdhvaṃ tato yānyarvāñcūrdhvamardharātrātsaṃveśanaṃ viṣṇuryoniṃ kalpayatvityetena tṛcena viṣṇuryoniṃ kalpayatu tvaṣṭā rūpāṇi piṃśatu /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Agni</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Candra</s> — you are the <s>prāyaścittas</s> (expiations) of the gods. A <s>brāhmaṇa</s> seeks your protection. Whatever form of hers destroys fame — remove that from her, <s>svāhā</s>!' Having offered a <s>sthālīpāka</s> (cooked oblation) to <s>Agni</s> and <s>Prajāpati</s>, having brought the remainders in a cup, one should say to her, 'Anoint your channels!' — [she anoints] the navel first, then what is above, then what is below. [They unite] after midnight. 'May <s>Viṣṇu</s> prepare the womb' — with this three-versed hymn: 'May <s>Viṣṇu</s> prepare the womb, may <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> fashion the forms,

children.text: āsiñcatu prajāpatirdhātā garbhaṃ dadhātu te //
children.translated_text: may <s>Prajāpati</s> pour forth, may <s>Dhātṛ</s> place the embryo in you.'

One blesses the departing [bride] with the verse '<s>Pūṣā</s> [shall lead] you hence': 'May <s>Pūṣan</s> lead you hence, taking you by the hand; may the <s>Aśvins</s> convey you on their chariot. Go to the house; be the mistress of the household; may you, having authority, preside over the assembly.' When she has arrived at her own [husband's] family, women of auspicious character and auspicious offspring, who have not lost their husbands, receive her. 'May joy be yours here; may you flourish with offspring in this house. Be wakeful for the <s>gārhapatya</s> (household fire). Unite your body with this husband; and when you are old, may you preside over the assembly.' Having received her, one seats her on a bull's hide with the hair upward: 'Let the cows sit down here, let the horses here, let the men here; let <s>Pūṣan</s> sit down here with a thousand gifts.' Having placed a boy-child on her lap, one scatters <s>śakalā</s> pebbles and fruits. Having then lifted the child, while she holds on [to the husband], one offers [eight oblations] ending with '<s>svāhā</s>' with the eight [mantras] beginning with 'Here is steadfastness': 'Here is steadfastness, here is self-possession, here is delight, here take delight! In me is steadfastness, in me is self-possession, in me is joy, in me take delight!' For three nights they sleep together as <s>brahmacārins</s> (celibates), eating food without pungent spices or salt, not lying on the ground, not having intercourse. After three nights, union takes place at night. At the rite of husband and wife, one should offer the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) oblations first — at the beginning of the expiation: 'You are the <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) of the gods, O <s>Agni</s>. I, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, seek your protection. Whatever form of hers destroys offspring — remove that from her, <s>svāhā</s>! You are the <s>prāyaścitta</s> of the gods, O <s>Vāyu</s>. I, a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, seek your protection. Whatever form of hers destroys cattle — remove that from her, <s>svāhā</s>!

children.text: garbhaṃ dhehi sinīvāligarbhaṃ dhehi sarasvati /
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Sinīvālī</s>, place the embryo; O <s>Sarasvatī</s>, place the embryo;

children.text: garbhaṃ te aśvinau devāvādhattāṃ puṣkarasrajau //
children.translated_text: may the two <s>Aśvin</s> gods, wearing lotus garlands, place the embryo in you!'

children.text: hiraṇyayī araṇī yaṃ nirmanthatāmāśvinau /
children.translated_text: 'The golden fire-sticks which the two <s>Aśvins</s> churned out —

children.text: taṃ te garbhaṃ dadhāmyahaṃ daśame māsi sūtavā ityṛtāvṛtāvevameva saṃveśane hutvācāryāya gāṃ dadyādadarśane brāhmaṇebhyo gāṃ dadyāti // JaimGS_1.22 //
children.translated_text: that embryo I place in you, for delivery in the tenth month.' In each fertile season, in exactly this manner, having offered at the time of union, one should give a cow to the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher). At the non-appearance [of menses, i.e., conception], one should give a cow to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>. // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.22 //

children.text: JaimGS 1.23:
children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 1.23:

children.text: sāyaṃprātarheme 'gnaya iti prathamāmāhutiṃ juhoti prajāpataya ityuttarāmevaṃ prātaragnisthāne sūryaḥ sāyaṃprātaraśanasya balī vardhayitvā pūrvasmādagnau juhotyagnaye svāhā somāya svāhā dhanvantaraye svāhā dyāvāpṛthvībhyāṃ svāhā viśvebhyo devebhyaḥ svāhā sarvābhyo devatābhyaḥ svāhā prajāpateya svāheti manasottarāṃ tata evottarato 'gnerbaliṃ harati ye harṣaṇā vepanā sphātimāharā vātasya bhrājamanusaṃcaranti /
children.translated_text: At the evening and morning oblation: 'O <s>Agni</s>' — thus one offers the first oblation; 'To <s>Prajāpati</s>' — the second. Similarly in the morning, the sun takes the place of <s>Agni</s>. Having increased the evening and morning food oblation, one offers into the earlier [established] fire: '<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Agni</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Soma</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Dhanvantari</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s> (Heaven and Earth)! <s>Svāhā</s> to the <s>Viśvedevas</s> (All-gods)! <s>Svāhā</s> to all deities! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Prajāpati</s>!' — the last one mentally. Then, from the same [fire], to the north of the fire, one carries out the <s>bali</s> (food-offering): 'Those who are exhilarating, trembling, who bring abundance, who move following the breath of the wind —

children.text: tebhyo balimannakāmo harāmyannaṃ payasvadbahulaṃ me astvityevamaśanāyatyāyasthāne mṛtyoradhiṣṭhānāya svāheti śeṣasya baliharaṇaṃ pradakṣiṇaṃ gṛhyābhyo devatābhyo baliṃ nayāmi tanme juṣantāṃ tā mā pāntu tā mā gopāyantu tā mā rakṣantu tābhyo namastābhyaḥ svāhetyudadhāne madhye 'gārasyauttarapūrvārdhe śayane dehalyāṃ saṃvaraṇe brahmāyatana eteṣvāyataneṣu śeṣaṃ dhanvantaraye ninayetsadā gṛheṣu svastivācanaṃ sā mahāśāntirityācakṣate // JaimGS_1.23 //
children.translated_text: to them, desiring food, I offer this <s>bali</s>; may my food be milky and abundant!' Thus one eats. At the place of rest, [one offers]: '<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Mṛtyu</s> (Death) for his station!' The carrying of the remainder of the <s>bali</s> [is done] clockwise: 'I carry the <s>bali</s> to the domestic deities; may they be pleased with me; may they protect me; may they guard me; may they shelter me. Homage to them, <s>svāhā</s> to them!' [One deposits the offerings] at the water-jar, in the middle of the house, in the northeastern quarter, at the bed, at the threshold, at the enclosure, and at the place of <s>Brahman</s>. At these stations, one directs the remainder to <s>Dhanvantari</s>. There should always be a <s>svastivācana</s> (benediction) in the house — this they call the <s>mahāśānti</s> (great pacification). // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.23 //

children.text: JaimGS 1.24:
children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 1.24:

children.text: navena yakṣyamāṇaḥ purāṇenāgre yajetāgnidhanvantarī prajāpatimindraṃ tisraśca navāhutīrnavena yajeta śaradi vrīhīṇāṃ vasante yavānāṃ varṣāsu śyāmākānāmaindrāgnau vaiśvadevo dyāvāpṛthivyaścarava ekacarurvokte evopastaraṇābhidhāraṇe dvirhaviṣe 'vadyatyatha prāśnīyādbhadrānnaḥ śreyaḥ samanaiṣṭa devāstvayāvasena samaśīmahi tvā /
children.translated_text: One who is about to offer with new [grain] should first offer with old [grain] — to <s>Agni</s>, <s>Dhanvantari</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and three additional nine oblations. One offers with new [grain]: in autumn with rice, in spring with barley, in the rainy season with <s>śyāmāka</s> (millet). [The oblation is] to <s>Indra-Agni</s>, <s>Vaiśvadeva</s>, and <s>Dyāvāpṛthivī</s>. One cooking pot [is used]. The preparation and anointing are as previously described. One cuts the <s>havis</s> twice. Then one should eat: 'The gods have sought for us what is auspicious and better; with the aftergrowth (<s>yavasa</s>) may we partake of you;

children.text: sa no mayobhūḥ pito āviśsva śaṃ tokāya tanuṣe syo ityetamu tyaṃ madhunā saṃyutaṃ yavaṃ sarasvatyā adhi manāvacarkṛṣuḥ /
children.translated_text: be gracious to us, O nourishing one, enter us; be beneficial for our offspring and our body.' And: 'This barley mixed with honey, on the banks of <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Manu</s> has cultivated;

children.text: indra āsītsīrapatiḥ śatakratuḥ kīnāśā āsanmarutaḥ sudānava iti yavasya prāśnīyādagniḥ prathamaḥ prāśnātu sa hi veda yathā haviḥ /
children.translated_text: <s>Indra</s> was the lord of the plow, <s>Śatakratu</s>; the plowmen were the <s>Maruts</s>, bountiful givers.' One should eat of the barley [saying]: 'May <s>Agni</s>, the foremost, eat first, for he knows the nature of the oblation; may he make the herbs auspicious for us, for all people.' One should eat of the <s>śyāmāka</s> (millet) [saying this].

children.text: śivā asmabhyamoṣadhīḥ kṛṇotu viśvacarṣaṇīriti śyāmākasya prāśnīyātprāśnīyāt // JaimGS_1.24 //
children.translated_text: One should eat. // <s>JaimGS</s> 1.24 //

children.text: // iti jaiminisūtraṃ pūrvam //
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first [book] of the <s>Jaimini Sūtra</s>.

children.text: JaimGS 2.1:
children.translated_text: <s>JaimGS</s> 2.1:

children.text: śrāddhaṃ kariṣyantaḥ snātāḥ śucivāsasastilairvāstvavakīrya savyamācaranto 'nnamupasādhayeranhaviṣyairupasicyaivaivaṃ dadyādyadyaddadyāttattaddhaviṣyairupasicyaiva haviṣyā iti tilānāmākhyā dantadhāvanaṃ snānīyāni pādyamānīya prathamoddhṛtaṃ brāhmaṇāṃstryavadātānupaveśayatyā me gacchantu pitaro bhāgadheyaṃ virājāhūtāḥ salilātsamudriyāt /
children.translated_text: Those about to perform the <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestor rite), having bathed, wearing clean garments, having scattered sesame seeds on the ground, performing rituals with the left hand, should prepare food. Having mixed it with <s>haviṣya</s> (pure/fit for oblation) ingredients — whatever one gives should be mixed with <s>haviṣya</s> ingredients. '<s>Haviṣya</s>' is the designation of sesame seeds. Teeth-cleaning, bathing materials, foot-water, and drinking water [are provided]. One seats three <s>brāhmaṇas</s> of pure character, invited first: 'May my ancestors come to me for their share, summoned in the <s>Virāj</s> [meter], from the ocean of waters.'

children.text: akṣīyamāṇamupajīvatainanmayā prattaṃ svadhayā madadhvamityupamūlalūnāndarbhānviṣṭarānprasavyānkṛtvā brāhmaṇebhyaḥ pradadyādetatte pitarāsanamasau ye ca tvātrānu tebhyaścāsanamityevaṃ pitāmahāyaivaṃ prapitāmahāya haviṣyodakaṃ tiraḥ pavitraṃ gandhānsumanasaśca dadyādannamavattvā ghṛtenābhidhārya darbhānparistaraṇīyāniti tadādāyāgnau kariṣyāmīti brāhmaṇānanujñāpya prāgdakṣiṇāmukho 'gniṃ praṇayitvā trirdhūnvanpradakṣiṇamagniṃ paristṛṇāti prācīnāvīti triḥ prasavyaṃ triḥ paryukṣetpradakṣiṇaṃ prācīnāvīti triḥ prasavyamaudumbara idhmaḥ paridhayo bhavanti mekṣaṇaṃ ca pavitraṃ saṃskṛtyānnamutpūyāgnau pavitraṃ prāsya mekṣaṇena juhotyagnaye kavyavāhanāya svadhā namaḥ svāhā somāya pitṛmate svadhā nama svāheti yajñopavīti bhūtvāpa upaspṛśya yamāyāṅgiḥsvate svāheti mekṣaṇamagrāvanupraharati namaskārānkṛtvā yathādaivataṃ triḥ paryukṣetpradakṣiṇaṃ prācīnāvīti triḥ prasavyaṃ savyañjanamannaṃ pātreṣu vardhayitvāmāsu pakvamiti kṣīraṃ ghṛtaṃ vā siñcatyāmāsu pakvamamṛtaṃ niviṣṭaṃ mayā prattaṃ svadhayā madadhvamiti vardhitānyādiśatyetadvaḥ pitaro bhāgadheyaṃ pātreṣu dattamamṛtaṃ svadhāvat /
children.translated_text: 'Inexhaustible, may you live upon this; offered by me, rejoice with <s>svadhā</s> (ancestral offering-call)!' Having cut <s>darbha</s> grass near the root and made it into seats (<s>viṣṭaras</s>) placed to the left, one should give them to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>: 'This is your seat, O father so-and-so, and for those who follow you here — for them also a seat.' Likewise for the grandfather, likewise for the great-grandfather. One should give sacrificial water through the <s>pavitra</s> (purifying grass), along with perfumes and flowers. Having portioned out the food and poured ghee over it, [saying] 'These <s>darbha</s> blades are for strewing around' — taking that up, [saying] 'I shall offer in the fire,' having obtained the permission of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, facing northeast, having kindled the fire, shaking three times, one strews [<s>darbha</s> grass] around the fire clockwise. With the sacred thread worn on the left (<s>prācīnāvītin</s>), three times counter-clockwise, one sprinkles around clockwise, [then] with the sacred thread on the left, three times counter-clockwise. The <s>idhma</s> (fuel-stick) and <s>paridhis</s> (enclosing sticks) are of <s>udumbara</s> (fig) wood. Having consecrated the <s>mekṣaṇa</s> (stirring-spoon) and <s>pavitra</s>, having purified the food, having cast the <s>pavitra</s> into the fire, one offers with the <s>mekṣaṇa</s>: 'To <s>Agni Kavyavāhana</s> (carrier of offerings to ancestors), <s>svadhā</s>, homage, <s>svāhā</s>! To <s>Soma Pitṛmat</s> (accompanied by the ancestors), <s>svadhā</s>, homage, <s>svāhā</s>!' Having put on the sacred thread (<s>yajñopavītin</s>), having touched water, [one offers] 'To <s>Yama Aṅgiras</s>, <s>svāhā</s>!' — one throws the <s>mekṣaṇa</s> after [the oblation]. Having made obeisances according to the deity, one sprinkles around three times clockwise, [then] with the sacred thread on the left, three times counter-clockwise. Having heaped up food with condiments in the vessels, one pours milk or ghee [saying]: 'Cooked in these [vessels], <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) has entered; offered by me, rejoice with <s>svadhā</s>!' One designates the heaped [offerings]: 'This is your portion, O ancestors, given in the vessels, nectar accompanied by <s>svadhā</s>.'

children.text: akṣīyamāṇamupajīvatainanmayā prattaṃ svadhayā madadhvam //
children.translated_text: 'Inexhaustible, may you live upon this; offered by me, rejoice with <s>svadhā</s>!'

children.text: amṛtā vāgamṛtā vāco agne vāco 'mṛtaḥ tvaṃ trivṛtaikadhāmā /
children.translated_text: Immortal is speech, immortal are words; O <s>Agni</s>, you are the immortal of speech, of threefold form, of one abode.

children.text: ebhirmatprattaiḥ svadhayā madadhvamihāsmabhyaṃ vasīyo 'stu devāḥ //
children.translated_text: By these [offerings] given by me, rejoice with <s>svadhā</s>! May there be greater prosperity for us here, O gods!

children.text: ayaṃ yajñaḥ paramo yaḥ pitṛṇāṃ pātradeyaṃ pitṛdaivatyamagne /
children.translated_text: This is the supreme sacrifice which belongs to the ancestors — the vessel-offering, O <s>Agni</s>, whose deity is the ancestors.

children.text: vākca manaśca pitaro naḥ prajānīmāśvibhyāṃ prattaṃ svadhayā madadhvam //
children.translated_text: Speech and mind — may our ancestors know [them]; offered by the two <s>Aśvins</s>, rejoice with <s>svadhā</s>!

children.text: ya iha pitaraḥ pārthivāso ya antarikṣa uta ye samudriyāḥ /
children.translated_text: Those ancestors who are here on earth, those who are in the atmosphere, and those who are in the ocean,

children.text: ye vācamāptvā amṛtā babhūvuste 'sminsarve haviṣi mādayantām //
children.translated_text: those who, having attained speech, became immortal — may they all rejoice in this oblation!

children.text: eṣā va ūrgeṣā vaḥ svadhā cāmatta ca pibata ca mā ca vaḥ kṣeṣṭa /
children.translated_text: This is your nourishment, this is your <s>svadhā</s>; eat and drink, and may it not be exhausted for you!

children.text: svadhāṃ vahadhvamamṛtasya yoniṃ yātra svadhā pitarastāṃ bhajadhvam //
children.translated_text: Bear the <s>svadhā</s>, the source of immortality! Where there is <s>svadhā</s>, O ancestors, resort to that!

children.text: yeha pitara ūrgdevatā ca tasyai jīvema śaradaḥ śataṃ vayam /

jyotiṣmaddhattājaraṃ ma āyurityathaitāni brāhmaṇebhya upanikṣipya svāṅguṣṭhenānuśatyamuṣmai svadhāmuṣmai svadheti yanme 'prakāmā iti bhuñjato 'numantrayate yanme 'prakāmā uta vā prakāmā samṛddhe brāhmaṇe 'brāhmaṇe vā /
children.translated_text: 'Grant [us] radiant, unaging life and longevity!' Thus, having placed these [offerings] before the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, one anoints with one's own thumb: 'To so-and-so, <s>svadhā</s>! To so-and-so, <s>svadhā</s>!' While they eat, one recites the blessing: 'Whatever of mine is insufficient or whatever is sufficient, [whether] among the prosperous <s>brāhmaṇas</s> or the non-<s>brāhmaṇas</s> —'

children.text: ya skandati nirṛtiṃ vāta ugrāṃ yena naḥ prīyante pitaro devatāśca /
children.translated_text: 'whatever spills out toward fierce <s>Nirṛti</s> (destruction), and that by which our ancestors and gods are pleased —'

children.text: vāyuṣṭatsarvaṃ śundhatu tena śuddhena devatā mādayantāṃ tasmiñchuddhe pitaro mādayantāmityakrānsamudra ityāśvaṃ gītvā saṃpannaṃ pṛṣṭāthācāmayedyajñopavītī bhūtvābhiramantāṃ bhavanta ityutkā pridakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā yanme rāmeti gacchanto 'numantrayate yanme rāmā śakuniḥ śvāpadaśca yanme 'śucirmantrakṛtasya prāśat /
children.translated_text: 'may <s>Vāyu</s> (Wind) purify all that; by that purified, may the gods rejoice; in that purified, may the ancestors rejoice!' Having sung '<s>Akrān samudra</s>' ('The ocean swelled') as a horse-[chant], [saying] 'It is accomplished,' having inquired, one should perform <s>ācamana</s> (water-sipping). Having put on the sacred thread, [saying] 'May you be delighted!' — having made a firebrand (<s>ulkā</s>) and circumambulated clockwise, while [the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>] depart, one recites the blessing: 'Whatever of mine is pleasant, [whatever] bird or wild animal, whatever impure thing has eaten of that which was prepared with <s>mantras</s> —'

children.text: vaiśvānaraḥ savitā tatpunātu tena pūtena devatā mādayantāṃ tasminpūte pitaro mādayantāmiti // JaimGS_2.1 //
children.translated_text: 'may <s>Vaiśvānara</s> <s>Savitṛ</s> purify that; by that purified, may the gods rejoice; in that purified, may the ancestors rejoice!' // JaimGS 2.1 //
Those ancestors who are here, who are nourishment-deities — by that [nourishment] may we live a hundred autumns!

children.translated_text: JaimGS 2.2:

children.translated_text: Having taken leave of the remainder, having returned, having smeared a four-cornered [space] extending east and south with cow-dung, [saying] 'Driven away are the <s>asuras</s>, <s>rākṣasas</s>, <s>piśācas</s>, and those seated among the ancestors!' — in the middle, one draws a line with a stick: 'Those who, assuming forms, being <s>asuras</s>, move about with <s>svadhā</s>, those who carry away, those who bear forth — may he drive them away from this world!' One places a firebrand (<s>ulmuka</s>) to the south along the line. Having strewn <s>darbha</s> grass, one performs <s>ācamana</s> with a water-vessel: 'Sip, O father so-and-so, and those who follow you here — may they also sip!' Likewise for the grandfather, likewise for the great-grandfather. On those [seats], one places the <s>piṇḍas</s> (rice-balls), [offering them] by name with the left hand: 'This is for you, O father so-and-so, and for those who follow you here — to them also, <s>svadhā</s>, homage!' Likewise for the grandfather, likewise for the great-grandfather. If the names are unknown: 'This is for the fathers; this is for the grandfathers; this is for the great-grandfathers.' If the lineage is unknown: 'This is for the ancestors dwelling on earth; this is for the grandfathers dwelling in the atmosphere; this is for the great-grandfathers dwelling in heaven.' [Saying] 'Here, O ancestors, rejoice! Each according to your share, satisfy yourselves!' — turning northward, one sits until they are satiated [thinking]: 'The ancestors have been satisfied, each according to their share, and have been gratified.' Having recited [this], one performs <s>ācamana</s> as before. Having loosened the lower garment (<s>nīvī</s>) and made obeisances according to the deity, [one says] 'This is here below, O ancestors!' and designates the garments: 'A tuft of wool, or a hem of cloth.' [Saying] 'This is here below, O ancestors — garments! Receive [them], O ancestors! Bestow upon us, O ancestors — bestow progeny, a child wearing a lotus-garland, such that there may be a man here!' One gives collyrium and ointment: 'Anoint yourself, so-and-so!' — 'Anoint yourself, so-and-so!' One should give perfumes and flowers. [Then] one worships with six obeisances beginning with 'Homage to you, ancestors!': 'Homage to you, ancestors! Homage to you, ancestors, for your vigor! Homage to you, ancestors, for your life-force! Homage to you, ancestors, for your fierceness! Homage to you, ancestors, for your strength! Homage to you, ancestors, for your wrath! To <s>svadhā</s> and to the ancestors, homage to you!' [Reciting] 'Bearing nourishment, <s>amṛta</s>, ghee, milk, <s>kīlāla</s> (sweet drink), and strained [<s>soma</s>] — you are <s>svadhā</s>; satisfy my ancestors!' — having poured out water, having consecrated it with 'May it not be exhausted for me' — [reciting] 'May it not be exhausted for me; may my meritorious deeds be abundant! May the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> be pleased with me! Food upon food!'

children.text: sahasradhāramamṛtodakaṃ me pūrtamastvetatparame vyoman //
children.translated_text: 'The thousand-streamed, immortal water — may my merit be in the highest heaven!'

children.text: devāśca pitaraścaitatpūrtaṃ me atropajīvantām /
children.translated_text: 'May the gods and ancestors live upon this merit of mine here!'

children.text: akṣīyamāṇamupajīvatainanmayā prattaṃ svadhayā madadhvamiti ye samānāḥ sumanasa iti pradakṣiṇaṃ kṛtvā ye samānāḥ sumanaso jīvā jīveṣu māmakāḥ /
children.translated_text: 'Inexhaustible, may you live upon this; offered by me, rejoice with <s>svadhā</s>!' [Saying] 'Those of like mind who are well-disposed' — having circumambulated clockwise — 'Those of like mind who are well-disposed, the living among the living, who are mine —'

children.text: teṣāṃ śrīrmayi kalpatāmasmiṃlloke śataṃ samā ityāmayāvī piṇḍānprāśnīyādannādyakāmo vāgnau vā saṃkṣepayedapsu vābhyamahareyurajaṃ gāṃ brāhmaṇaṃ vā prāśayeyuḥ śeṣasya prāśnīyānna cānnatṛptiṃ gacchet // JaimGS_2.2 //
children.translated_text: 'may their prosperity accrue to me; may we live a hundred years in this world!' A sick person should eat the <s>piṇḍas</s>; or one desiring food-abundance [should eat them]; or one may throw them into the fire or into water. Or, a hornless cow, or a goat, or a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> may be fed [with them]. One should eat the remainder, but should not reach complete satiation from food. // JaimGS 2.2 //

children.text: ūrdhvamāgrahāyaṇyāstrayo 'parapakṣāsteṣāmekaikasminnekaikāṣṭakā bhavati śākāṣṭakā māṃsāṣṭakāpūpāṣṭaketi tatra śākamāṃsāpūpāni havīṃṣyodanaṃ ca teṣāṃ haviṣāṃ sthālīpākāvṛtāgnau juhuyādaṣṭakāyai svāhā ekāṣṭakārye svāhā aṣṭakāyai surādhase svāhā saṃvatsarāya parivatsarāyedāvatsarāyedvatsarāya kṛṇutā nāmobhiḥ /
children.translated_text: After the <s>Āgrahāyaṇī</s> (full moon of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>), there are three dark fortnights; in each of these, there is one <s>Aṣṭakā</s> (eighth-day) [festival] — the Vegetable <s>Aṣṭakā</s>, the Meat <s>Aṣṭakā</s>, and the Cake <s>Aṣṭakā</s>. There, vegetables, meat, and cakes are the oblation-materials, along with rice. Of those oblation-materials, offerings are made in the <s>sthālīpāka</s> (cooked offering) fire: '<s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Aṣṭakā</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to the supreme <s>Aṣṭakā</s>! <s>Svāhā</s> to <s>Aṣṭakā Surādhasa</s> (bestower of liquor)! To <s>Saṁvatsara</s> (the Year), <s>Parivatsara</s>, <s>Idāvatsara</s>, <s>Idvatsara</s> — 'Make [obeisances] with homage!'

children.text: tvayā vayaṃ sumatau yajñiyānāṃ jyogajītā ahatāḥ syāma svāheti hutvopatiṣṭhata ehi bhagaihi bhagaihi bhageti madhyamāyāṃ gāṃ kārayettāmaṣṭakāyai prokṣettasyāstrīṇi savyānyupoddharati pārśvamapaghanīṃ śroṇīmiti śvobhūte śrāddhamanvaṣṭakyaṃ tadaharvā brāhmaṇānhavirarhānupaveśya tāṃstarpayitvā tasmādagrerdakṣiṇataḥ ṣaḍagrīnpraṇīya teṣāmekaikasminnekaikāṃ karṣūkhānayedāyāmena prādeśamātrīṃ pārthivena tryaṅgulāmavāgvaikāṅgulāmiti tāsu piṇḍānnidadhātyanunāmāpahastena mañjāḥ pitṛbhya upakarṣati pārśvāni strīṇāṃ tatrādhvaryavaḥ kecidadhīyate madhyamaṃ piṇḍaṃ patnī prāśnīyātprajākāmasya tathā śrāddhasya sthālīpākaṃ vā śrāddhasya sthālīpākaṃ vā // JaimGS_2.3 //
children.translated_text: 'May we, in your favor, among those worthy of sacrifice, long undefeated and unharmed, [live in prosperity], <s>svāhā</s>!' Having offered, one worships: 'Come, O <s>Bhaga</s> (Fortune)! Come, O <s>Bhaga</s>! Come, O <s>Bhaga</s>!' On the middle [<s>Aṣṭakā</s>], one should have a cow prepared; one should consecrate her for <s>Aṣṭakā</s>. Three left [portions] are extracted from her: the side, the hip-bone, and the haunch. The next day is the <s>Anvaṣṭakya</s> <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite following the <s>Aṣṭakā</s>) — or on that very day. Having seated <s>brāhmaṇas</s> worthy of the oblation and having satiated them, from that [altar's] tip southward, having placed six tips [of <s>darbha</s>] pointing south, in each of them one should dig a small pit (<s>karṣū</s>) — a span in length, three fingers wide in the earthen [dimension], one finger deep downward. In those, one places the <s>piṇḍas</s> (rice-balls), [offering] by name with the left hand. The <s>mañjā</s> (marrow-portions) are drawn toward the ancestors; the side-portions toward the women [ancestors]. Therein some <s>Adhvaryu</s> priests recite [additionally]. The wife should eat the middle <s>piṇḍa</s> if desiring offspring. Likewise for the <s>śrāddha</s>: a <s>sthālīpāka</s> [is offered]. Or a <s>sthālīpāka</s> for the <s>śrāddha</s>. // JaimGS 2.3 //

children.text: āhitāgneḥ śarīranāśe trīṇi ṣaṣṭiśatāni palāśatsarūṇāmāhṛtya taiḥ pratikṛtiṃ kuryātkṛṣṇājine 'śītyardhaṃ śirasi dadhyādgrīvāyāṃ tu daśaiva tu bāhvoścaiva śataṃ dadhyātaṅguliṣu punardaśā urasi triṃśataṃ dadhyājjaṭhare viṃśatīṃ tathorvoścaiva śataṃ dadhyāt meḍhre cāpi daśaiva tu jānujaṃghayostriṃśata dadhyāt daśa pādāṅgulīṣvapi ityetāvantīha puruṣasya śarīrāṇi bhavantīti vijñāyate madhye śarīraṃ satīśarīramuptakeśaṃ nikṛttanakhaṃ prakṣālitaṃ citāmāropayantyatra pātrāṇyapi cinoti tasyāmenamādadhati tasya nāsikayoḥ sruvau nidadhyādityetenānuvākena ya evaṃvitsyātsa yadopatāpī syāditi pūrvameva caturgṛhītaṃ gṛhītvānyaṃ yathāsaṃbhavamāsye hiraṇyaśakalamamādhāyāgnīnupohya sāmabhirupatiṣṭhate nāke suparṇamiti grāmyaṃ geyamudite dhūme tveṣaste dhūma ṛṇvatītyagnau samārūḍhe 'gne mṛḍa mahaṃ asītyetayoranyatareṇa parāk parāgvā asau loka iti brāhmaṇam // JaimGS_2.4 //
children.translated_text: When the body of one who has maintained the sacred fires (<s>āhitāgni</s>) is lost [i.e., cannot be found], one should bring three hundred and sixty <s>palāśa</s> (butea) twigs and make an effigy with them on a black antelope skin: eighty-half [i.e., forty] should be placed on the head, ten on the neck, a hundred on the two arms, another ten on the fingers, thirty on the chest, twenty on the belly, a hundred on the two thighs, and ten on the male organ, thirty on the knees and shanks, and ten on the toes. 'This many are the bodily parts of a person' — so it is known. The body in the middle is the real body — with hair pulled out, nails cut, washed — they place it on the funeral pyre. There too one arranges the ritual vessels. One places him on it. One should place the two <s>sruvas</s> (ladles) at his nostrils — thus by this <s>anuvāka</s> (section). He who knows thus, when he becomes afflicted — having first taken the four-fold [offering], and another as available, having placed a gold chip in the mouth, having piled up the fires, one recites <s>sāmans</s>: 'The eagle in heaven' — a village melody should be sung. When the smoke rises: 'Your smoke is fierce, resounding.' When [the body] is mounted on the fire: 'O <s>Agni</s>, be gracious, you are great' — with one or the other of these. Turning away: 'Yonder is the other world' — this is the <s>brāhmaṇa</s> [teaching]. // <s>JaimGS</s> 2.4 //

children.text: āhitāgneśvetpūrvaṃ jāyā mriyeta tāṃ nirmanthyena dahetsāṃtapanena vā śmaśānakṛtaṃ svakṛtamaniriṇamapasalavakrodakaṃ kṛtvā yatra vauṣadhayo jāyante tatra śarīraṃ dagdhvodakakaraṇāya yāntyanavekṣamāṇā na vāhinīṣu kurvanti teṣāṃ yoyaḥ paścāñjātaḥ saso 'graṃ kuryādupakūlamakūle kūpaṃ khātvā savyahastasyānāmikayā sakṛdudakaṃ prohati pretasya nāmakaraṇena vāhinīṣu cedudgrathya keśānnimajyaikāñjaliṃ dattvopasaṃgṛhya keśānulmukasyāgnimārabhetāgre śūkāhe pāpaṃ me 'pahateti śamīmārabheta śamyasi śamaya me pāpamityaśmānamārabhetāśmāsi sthiro 'syahaṃ sthiro bhūyāsamiti tūṣṇīṃ gomayaṃ kṛtodakaṃ dakṣiṇāmukhamāsīnaṃ tamanugantāra upaviśanti tānitaraḥ kalyāṇībhirvāgbhiḥ pratyāhopāstamanavelāyāṃ grāmaṃ praviśanti tāṃ rātrimekamāṣeṇa vasanti śāntyā vā śvo bhūte kṣīrodake saṃsṛjya śarīrāṇyavasiñcatyajaśṛṅgeṇa gośṛṅgena mṛṇamayena kośena vā tṛtīyāyāṃ gandhauṣadhībhiḥ saṃsṛjya śamīśākhayā palāśaśākhayā vāsaṃhlādayankumbhyāmavadadhyātstrī cedvaṭa eva dadhyāccatuṣpathamatītya mahāvṛkṣaṃ nadīṃ vā tīrtheṣu nikhanet pretasya tṛtīyāyāṃ snāpayantyapāmārgeṇa mṛdā gomayena ca vāsāṃsi prakṣālya daśarātramāsate caturthyāṃ bhikṣāmāvartayerantasya siddhamagnaukaraṇaṃ kālaṃ ca yāvadākāṃkṣeyurbhikṣayānusaṃtareyurūrdhvaṃ daśarātrācchrāddhaṃ dadyurna dadyurā śrāddhasya pradānānnakṣatreṣu niyamo madhāsvekatāreṣu bharaṇīṣu ca pūrvasamayeṣu na rehiṇayamuttareṣu dhruveṣu brāhmaṇānhavirarhānupaveśya tāṃstarpayitvaikavatpiṇḍaṃ dadyānna cānviti brūyātsarvaiḥ karmaistarpayedanugamanaṃ kṛtvā śeṣamanujñāpya pratyetya śeṣaṃ na prāśnīyādbrāhmaṇānsvasti vācya prāśnīyāt // JaimGS_2.5 //
children.translated_text: If the wife of one who has maintained the sacred fires dies first, one should cremate her with fire produced by churning (<s>nirmanthya</s>) or with the <s>sāṃtapana</s> fire. Having prepared a cremation ground — self-made, not a burial ground, on level ground free from saline soil, and near water — or where plants grow, one should cremate the body. Those who go for the water-rite go without looking back. They do not perform [the rite] in flowing rivers. Whoever among them is born last should go first. At a riverbank — not at a bank [but at a dug] well — with the ring finger of the left hand, one offers water once, calling the name of the deceased. If in flowing rivers, having tied up the hair, having immersed, having offered one handful, having grasped the hair, one should kindle fire from a firebrand. First, at the <s>śūkāha</s>: 'Remove my sin!' Then one should grasp a <s>śamī</s> branch: 'You are the <s>śamī</s>; pacify my sin.' Then one should grasp a stone: 'You are a stone; you are firm; may I become firm.' Silently, [one touches] cow-dung. Having made the water-offering, [the mourners] sit facing south. The followers sit around him. Someone comforts them with auspicious words. At the time of sunset, they enter the village. That night they subsist on a single portion of black beans — or with a <s>śānti</s> (pacification) [rite]. The next day, having mixed the bones (<s>śarīrāṇi</s>) with milk and water, one sprinkles them with a goat's horn, a cow's horn, or a clay cup. On the third day, having mixed with fragrant herbs, using a <s>śamī</s> branch or a <s>palāśa</s> branch, one should refresh [the bones] and place them in a pot. If a woman, one should place them in a fig tree. Having passed a crossroads and [reached] a great tree or a river, one should bury them at sacred fords — of the deceased. On the third day, one bathes [the mourners] with <s>apāmārga</s> plant, clay, and cow-dung. Having washed the garments, they sit for ten days. On the fourth day, they resume begging for food. The cooked offering and fire-rite for the deceased are ready. For as long as they desire, they may sustain themselves by begging. After ten days, they should offer a <s>śrāddha</s> — or they may not. Until the offering of the <s>śrāddha</s>, there is observance [of mourning] on [specific] <s>nakṣatras</s> (lunar asterisms) — in the months of <s>Māgha</s>, on single-starred ones, on <s>Bharaṇī</s>, and in the former half [of the month]. The <s>Rohiṇī</s> is not [suitable] for the latter; on the fixed [asterisms]. Having seated <s>brāhmaṇas</s> worthy of oblations, having satisfied them, one should give a single <s>piṇḍa</s> (rice ball). One should not say 'Follow!' (<s>anu</s>). One should satisfy [the deceased] with all rites. Having performed the following-procession and having taken leave of the remainder, having returned, one should not eat the remainder. Having pronounced benedictions for the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, one may eat. // <s>JaimGS</s> 2.5 //

children.text: athāto gṛhakarmaṇo gṛhavṛddhimicchanmāsimāsyūtāvṛtau saṃvatsare saṃvatsare vā pūrvapakṣe puṇye nakṣatre gṛhaśāntimārabhetāpāmārgapalāśaśirīpākāraidumbaralasadābhadrāmṛtatṛṇamindravallībhirbaddhvā gṛhānparimārjya parisamūhyāpo 'bhyukṣya pañcagavyairdarbhamuṣṭinā saṃprokṣya siddhārthakānsaṃprakīrya vāstubaliṃ kṛtvā vāstormadhye vāstoṣpattiṃ hutvā sāvitryā sahasraṃ juhuyāttato dakṣiṇapurastāttato dakṣiṇāpaścāttata uttarapurastāttata uttarapaścānmadhye vā gaurvāso hiraṇyaṃ dakṣiṇā brāhmaṇānannena pariviṣyaṃ puṇyāhaṃ svastyuddhimiti vācayitvaivaṃ prayuñjāno 'nantaṃ mahāntaṃ poṣaṃ puṣyati bahavaḥ putrā bhavanti na ca bālāḥ pramīyante nāgnirdahati na daṃṣṭriṇaḥ khādayeyurna taskarāḥ sapatnā rakṣāṃsi piśācā api bādhante yadi gāvaḥ pratapyerangavāṃ madhya āhutisahasraṃ juhuyādityetenaiva kalpenāścoṣṭrakharājāvikamahiṣahastikulamanyataraddvipadāṃ catuṣpadāṃ ca vyākhyātam // JaimGS_2.6 //
children.translated_text: Now, regarding the household rite: one who desires the prosperity of the house should, month by month, or season by season, or year by year, in the bright fortnight, on an auspicious <s>nakṣatra</s> (asterism), undertake the <s>gṛhaśānti</s> (house-pacification). Having bound [branches of] <s>apāmārga</s>, <s>palāśa</s>, <s>śirīṣa</s>, <s>pākāra</s>, <s>udumbara</s>, <s>lasad</s>, <s>ābhadra</s>, <s>amṛtatṛṇa</s> (immortality-grass), and <s>indravallī</s> (Indra's creeper), having swept and cleaned the house, having sprinkled it with water and the five products of the cow (<s>pañcagavya</s>), having aspersed with a handful of <s>darbha</s> grass, having scattered white mustard seeds, having made the <s>vāstubali</s> (house-offering), having offered to <s>Vāstoṣpati</s> (Lord of the Dwelling) in the middle of the house, one should offer a thousand oblations with the <s>Sāvitrī</s> [mantra] — then from the southeast, then from the southwest, then from the northeast, then from the northwest, or in the middle. A cow, a garment, and gold are the fee. Having served food to <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, having had them recite '<s>Puṇyāham</s>, <s>svasti</s>, <s>uddhi</s>' (auspiciousness, well-being, prosperity) — one who performs thus attains endless, great prosperity. Many sons are born and young ones do not die. Fire does not burn [the house], fanged creatures do not devour, thieves, rivals, <s>rākṣasas</s>, and <s>piśācas</s> do not harm. If cattle are ailing, one should offer a thousand oblations in the midst of the cattle. By this same procedure, [rites for] camels, donkeys, goats, sheep, buffaloes, and elephant herds — any of bipeds or quadrupeds — are explained. // <s>JaimGS</s> 2.6 //

sadasaspatimadbhutam /

children.translated_text: with the verse to <s>Prajāpati</s>, one offers from the front and from above with the <s>Mahāvyāhṛtis</s> (great sacred utterances). One chants these <s>Ṛc</s> and <s>Sāman</s> verses. // <s>JaimGS</s> 2.7 //

Now we shall explain the <s>adbhutaśānti</s> (pacification of portents). If a pillar sprouts in the house, or a pigeon enters the house, or a cow suckles another cow, or [something] scratches the sky without being called, or smoke arises without fire, or [something] blazes without fire, or honey appears, or an anthill grows up, or a frog croaks in an uncovered [vessel], or dogs roam about in the house — for these and other [portents], [one recites]: 'O <s>Indra</s>, from what we fear, O wondrous <s>Sadaspati</s> (Lord of the Assembly),

children.text: athāto 'naśnatsaṃhitāyāḥ kalpaṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ śucivāsāḥ syāccīravāsā vā haviṣyamannamaśanamicchedapaḥ phalāni vā brāhmaṇastveva pratyāharetprāṅ vodaṅ vā grāmānniṣkramya śucau deśa udakānte vā gomayena gocarmamātraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya prokṣya lakṣaṇamullikhyādbhirabhyukṣyāgnimupasamādhāyāghārāvājyabhāgau hutvājyāhutīrjuhotyagnaye somāya rudrāyendrāya brahmaṇe prajāpataye bṛhaspataye viśvebhyo devebhya ṛṣibhya ṛgbhyo yajurbhyaḥ sāmabhyaḥ śraddhāyai prajñāyai medhāyai sāvitryai sadasaspataye 'numataye ca hutvā durbheṣvāsīnaḥ prāktūleṣūdaktūleṣu vā dakṣiṇena pāṇinā darbhāndhārayannopūrvā vyāhṛtīḥ sāvitrīṃ ca caturanudrutya manasā sāmasāvitrīṃ ca somaṃ rājānaṃ brahmajajñānīye cobhe vedādimārabheta saṃtatamadhīyīta maunī na cāntarā viramet athāntaraḥ vyāharedathāntarā viramet trīnprāṇānāyamyatamyācamya vṛttāntādevārabhetāpratibhāyāṃ yāvatā kālena vedamadhīyīta tāvatkālamadhīyīta yajjānīyādṛkto yajuṣṭaḥ sāmatastadavāpnuyāttadbrāhmaṇaṃ tacchāndasaṃ taddaivataṃ sāma vā akānityetadeva vābhyasyettiṣṭhānnāsīnaḥ śayānaścaṅkramyamāṇo vā saṃhitāṃ prayuñjyātsamṛddhirevāsya bhavatyādyaṃ trivargaṃ vā sahasrakṛtva iti jaiminiśca vāryamantaṃ vā yathākāmī vā dvādaśa saṃhitā adhītya yadanenānadhyāyeṣvadhītaṃ yadguravaḥ kopitā yānyakāryāṇi kṛtāni tābhiḥ pavate śuddhamasya pūtaṃ brahma bhavatyathāparā dvādaśa saṃhitā adhītya tābhiḥ prajāpaterlokamavāpnotyanaśnatsaṃhitāsahasramadhītya brahmabhūto virajo bhavati kāmacārī sarvānkāmānavāpnoti saṃvatsaraṃ bhaikṣabhakṣaḥ prayuñjānaścakṣurlabhate ṣaṇmāsānyāvakabhakṣaścaturo etayā vai devā devatvamagacchannṛṣaya ṛṣitvaṃ tasya ha vā etasyā brahmasatrasya trividha evārabhyo bhavati prātaḥsavane mādhyaṃdine savane brāhme vāpararātre tasya ha vai etasya dvāvevānadhyāyau yadātmāśuciryaddeśastadvā etatprajāpatiḥ saptaṛṣibhyaḥ provāca saptaṛṣayo mahājahnave mahājahnurbrāhmaṇebhyo brāhmaṇebhyaḥ // JaimGS_2.8 //
children.translated_text: Now we shall explain the procedure for [reciting] the <s>Saṃhitā</s> while fasting. One should wear clean garments or bark garments. One should wish to eat <s>haviṣya</s> (pure) food — water or fruits. Only a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> should undertake this. Departing from the village eastward or northward, in a clean place or by the water's edge, having smeared a ground-altar the size of a cowhide with cow-dung, having sprinkled and marked it, having sprinkled with water, having built up the fire, having offered the two <s>āghāras</s> and the two <s>ājyabhāgas</s>, one offers <s>ājya</s> oblations: to <s>Agni</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, the <s>Viśvedevas</s>, the <s>Ṛṣis</s>, the <s>Ṛcs</s>, the <s>Yajus</s> formulas, the <s>Sāmans</s>, to <s>Śraddhā</s> (Faith), <s>Prajñā</s> (Wisdom), <s>Medhā</s> (Intelligence), <s>Sāvitrī</s>, <s>Sadaspati</s>, and <s>Anumatī</s>. Having offered, seated on <s>darbha</s> grass with tips pointing east or north, holding <s>darbha</s> grass in the right hand, one recites the <s>Vyāhṛtis</s> (sacred utterances) in order and the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, repeating four times mentally, and the <s>Sāma-Sāvitrī</s>, '<s>Somaṃ rājānam</s>' ('King <s>Soma</s>'), and both of the '<s>Brahmajajñānam</s>' ('Brahman was born of wisdom'). One should begin from the beginning of the <s>Veda</s> and study continuously, observing silence, without interruption. If one speaks in between, or if one interrupts, having performed three <s>prāṇāyāmas</s> (breath-controls) and sipped water (<s>ācamana</s>), one should resume from the point of interruption. In case of loss of memory, one should study for as long a time as it takes to complete the <s>Veda</s>. Whatever one knows from the <s>Ṛc</s>, the <s>Yajus</s>, or the <s>Sāman</s> — one obtains that: the <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>, the <s>Chandas</s>, and the <s>Daivata</s> (deity portions), or the <s>Sāman</s> without vowel marks — or one may practice just this. One may employ the <s>Saṃhitā</s> standing, not sitting, lying down, or walking. Prosperity indeed becomes his. [He obtains] the first three goals of life, or [he may recite] a thousand times — so [say] <s>Jaimini</s> and others — or ending with the <s>Vārya</s>, or as one desires. Having studied twelve <s>Saṃhitās</s>, whatever was studied during prohibited days, whatever offenses were committed against teachers, whatever improper acts were done — by these [recitations] one is purified; his <s>Brahman</s> becomes pure and cleansed. Then, having studied another twelve <s>Saṃhitās</s>, by those one attains the world of <s>Prajāpati</s>. Having studied a thousand <s>Saṃhitās</s> while fasting, one becomes <s>Brahman</s>, becomes free from impurity, moves freely, and attains all desires. [Practicing] for a year, subsisting on alms, one obtains [divine] sight; for six months, subsisting on barley; for four months, subsisting on water and ground grain; for two months, subsisting on fruits; for one month, subsisting on water; or for twelve days fasting — one quickly disappears [from the mortal world]. One purifies one's relatives — seven past and seven future — and oneself as the fifteenth, one saves. They call this the 'divine ladder' (<s>devaniśreṇī</s>). By this indeed the gods attained godhood and the <s>ṛṣis</s> attained the status of <s>ṛṣis</s>. Of this <s>brahmasatra</s> (divine session), there are three possible times to begin: at the morning pressing, at the midday pressing, or in the divine [time of] the latter part of the night. For this, there are only two prohibited days: when oneself is impure and when the place is [impure]. This indeed <s>Prajāpati</s> taught to the Seven <s>Ṛṣis</s>; the Seven <s>Ṛṣis</s> [taught it] to <s>Mahājahnu</s>; <s>Mahājahnu</s> to the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>; and the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> [transmitted it further]. // <s>JaimGS</s> 2.8 //

children.text:
atha grahāṇamātithyaṃ balikarmopurataṃ vyākhyāsyāmaḥ aśraddadhānamaśucikaraṇamajāpyaṃ tyaktamaṅgalaṃ /
suvyaktaṃ grahā nayanti /
puruṣaṃ yamasādanam /
grahāṇāṃ dīpraceṣṭānāṃ nakṣatrapathacāriṇām /
grahātithyaṃ pravakṣyāmi śāntikarmaṇi kārayet /
bhāskarāṅgārakau raktau śvetau śukaniśākarau /
somaputro guruścaiva tāvubhau pītako smṛtau /
kṛṣṇaṃ śanaiśvaraṃ vidyādrāhuṃ kretuṃ tathaiva ca /
grahavarṇāni puṣpāṇi prājñastatropakalpayet /
gomayena gocarmamātraṃ sthaṇḍilamupalipya prokṣya lakṣaṇamullikhyādbhirabhyukṣyāgnimupasamādhāyāṅārāvājyabhāgau hutvā grahānāvāhantyādityaṃ madhye lohitaṃ pūrvadakṣiṇataḥ somam /
pūrvottarato budhamuttareṇa guruṃ pūrveṇa bhārgavam /
paścime śanaiścaraṃ vidyādrāhuṃ dakṣiṇapaścime paścimottarataḥ ketuṃ vṛttamādityāya trikoṇamaṅgārakasya caturaśraṃ somāya bāṇaṃ budhāya dīrghacaturaśraṃ bṛhaspataye pañcakoṇaṃ śukrāya dhanuḥ śanaiścarāya rāhoḥ śūrpaṃ ketordhvajamiti īśvaraṃ bhāskaraṃ vidyāta umāṃ somaṃ tathaiva ca /
skandamaṅgārakaṃ caiva budho nārāyaṇaḥ sthitaḥ /
bṛhaspatiḥ svayaṃ brahma śukraḥ śakrastathaiva ca /
yamaṃ śanaiścaraṃ vidyādrāhoḥ kāladūtinaḥ ketościtraguptaścetyete grahadevatāḥ agnirāpo bhūmirviṣṇurindrāṇī prajāpatiḥ sarpo brahmetyete pratyadhidevatāḥ jātamarka kaliṅgeṣu yāmuneṣu ca candramāḥ /
vindhya aṅgārakadeśo madhyadeśo budhaḥ smṛtaḥ /
children.translated_text: the <s>Vindhya</s> is the region of <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars); <s>Madhyadeśa</s> (the central region) is regarded as <s>Budha</s>'s (Mercury's);

children.text: bṛhaspatiḥ sindhudeśaḥ śakradeśo ghaṭeṣu ca /
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter) [is associated with] the <s>Sindhu</s> region; the region of <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) is among the <s>Ghaṭas</s>;

children.text: śanaiścarastu saurāṣṭro rāhustu pūrvadeśikaḥ ketuḥ parvata ityete deśānāṃ grahajāta iti arkasamidhamādityāya prādeśamātrābhidhāritānāmyādibhirjuhuyāt khādiramaṅgārakāya pālāśaṃ somāyāpāmārgaṃ budhāyāśvatthaṃ bṛhaspataya audumbaraṃ śukrāya śamīṃ śanaiścarāya rāhordūrvāḥ ketoḥ kuśāgramityaṣṭāviṃśatimājyāhutīrjuhotyetābhiḥ pakvāgnerjuhotyādityāya ilodanaṃ haviṣyamannamaṅgārakāya somāya ghṛtapāyasaṃ payodanaṃ bṛhaspataye kṣīrodanaṃ śukrāya dadhyodanaṃ budhāya tilapiṣṭamāṣodanaṃ śanaiścarāya rāhormāṃsodanaṃ ketościtrodanamiti ā satyenetyādityāya agnirmūrdhā diva ityaṅgārakāya āpyāyasva sametu iti somāya brahma jajñānamiti budhāya bṛhaspate ati yadarya iti bṛhaspataye asya pratnāmanu dyutamiti śukrāya śaṃ no devīrabhiṣṭaya iti śanaiścarāya kayā naścitra ābhuvaditi rāhoḥ ketuṃ kṛṇavannaketava ithi ketoḥ raktaṃ dhenumādityāya raktamanaḍvāhamaṅgārakāya somāya śaṅkhaṃ budhāya kāñcanaṃ bṛhaspataye vāsaḥ śukrāya hayaṃ nīlāṃ gāṃ śanaiścarāya rāhoḥ kṛṣṇāyasaṃ ketoḥ kuñjaramiti sarveṣāmapi hiraṇyaṃ vā yena vā tuṣyatyācāryastaddadāti yathā samutthitaṃ yantraṃ yantreṇa pratihanyate /
children.translated_text: <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn) is of <s>Saurāṣṭra</s>; <s>Rāhu</s> is of the eastern region; <s>Ketu</s> is of the mountain region — these are the regional associations of the planets. The fuel-sticks for each, a span in length, to be offered with the prescribed <s>mantras</s>: <s>arka</s> wood for <s>Āditya</s> (Sun), <s>khadira</s> for <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars), <s>palāśa</s> for <s>Soma</s> (Moon), <s>apāmārga</s> for <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), <s>aśvattha</s> (fig) for <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter), <s>udumbara</s> for <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), <s>śamī</s> for <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), <s>dūrvā</s> grass for <s>Rāhu</s>, <s>kuśa</s>-grass tips for <s>Ketu</s>. Twenty-eight <s>ājya</s> (ghee) oblations are offered with these. The cooked food offerings for each: mixed rice (<s>ilodana</s>) as sacrificial food for <s>Āditya</s> (Sun), [sacrificial food] for <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars), ghee-milk-pudding (<s>ghṛtapāyasa</s>) for <s>Soma</s> (Moon), milk-rice (<s>payodana</s>) for <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter), milk-rice (<s>kṣīrodana</s>) for <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), curd-rice (<s>dadhyodana</s>) for <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), sesame-flour-and-black-lentil-rice (<s>tilapiṣṭamāṣodana</s>) for <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), meat-rice (<s>māṃsodana</s>) for <s>Rāhu</s>, and variegated rice (<s>citrodana</s>) for <s>Ketu</s>. The <s>mantras</s>: for <s>Āditya</s>, '<s>ā satyena</s>'; for <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, '<s>agnir mūrdhā divaḥ</s>'; for <s>Soma</s>, '<s>āpyāyasva sametu</s>'; for <s>Budha</s>, '<s>brahma jajñānam</s>'; for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, '<s>Bṛhaspate ati yad arya</s>'; for <s>Śukra</s>, '<s>asya pratnām anu dyutam</s>'; for <s>Śanaiścara</s>, '<s>śaṃ no devīr abhiṣṭaye</s>'; for <s>Rāhu</s>, '<s>kayā naś citra ābhuvat</s>'; for <s>Ketu</s>, '<s>ketuṃ kṛṇavann aketave</s>.' The <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (fee): a red cow for <s>Āditya</s>, a red bull for <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, a conch shell for <s>Soma</s>, gold for <s>Budha</s>, a garment for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, a horse for <s>Śukra</s>, a dark cow for <s>Śanaiścara</s>, iron for <s>Rāhu</s>, an elephant for <s>Ketu</s>. For all of them, [one may alternatively give] gold, or whatever pleases the <s>ācārya</s> (teacher) — that one gives. Just as a risen device is countered by a [counter-]device,

children.text: tathā grahopaspṛṣṭānāṃ śāntirbhavati dāruṇam //
children.translated_text: so too the terrible [effects] of those afflicted by planets are pacified.

Now we shall explain the hospitality rite for the planets (<s>grahātithya</s>) along with the <s>bali</s>-offering ritual. One who lacks faith, impure in action, who does not recite prayers, who has abandoned auspicious rites — clearly, the planets lead such a person to the abode of <s>Yama</s>. Of the planets, of brilliant activity, who traverse the path of the <s>nakṣatras</s> (constellations) — I shall declare the hospitality rite for the planets; one should have the pacification (<s>śānti</s>) ritual performed. <s>Bhāskara</s> (Sun) and <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars) are red; <s>Śukra</s> (Venus) and <s>Niśākara</s> (Moon) are white; <s>Somaputra</s> (Mercury) and <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) — both are regarded as yellow; one should know <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), <s>Rāhu</s>, and <s>Ketu</s> as dark. A wise person should arrange flowers of the corresponding colors for the planets. Having smeared a platform the size of a cowhide with cowdung, having sprinkled it, having drawn the diagram, having sprinkled it with water, having set up the fire and offered the two portions of <s>ājya</s> (ghee), they invoke the planets: <s>Āditya</s> (Sun) in the center, <s>Lohita</s> (Mars) in the southeast, <s>Soma</s> (Moon) in the northeast, <s>Budha</s> (Mercury) to the north, <s>Guru</s> (Jupiter) to the east, <s>Bhārgava</s> (Venus) to the west, <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn) one should know, <s>Rāhu</s> in the southwest, <s>Ketu</s> to the northwest. The diagram for <s>Āditya</s> is a circle, for <s>Aṅgāraka</s> a triangle, for <s>Soma</s> a square, for <s>Budha</s> an arrow, for <s>Bṛhaspati</s> a rectangle, for <s>Śukra</s> a pentagon, for <s>Śanaiścara</s> a bow, for <s>Rāhu</s> a winnowing basket, for <s>Ketu</s> a banner. The presiding deities: one should know <s>Īśvara</s> for <s>Bhāskara</s> (Sun), <s>Umā</s> for <s>Soma</s> (Moon), <s>Skanda</s> for <s>Aṅgāraka</s> (Mars), <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> presides over <s>Budha</s> (Mercury), <s>Brahmā</s> himself for <s>Bṛhaspati</s> (Jupiter), <s>Śakra</s> (Indra) for <s>Śukra</s> (Venus), one should know <s>Yama</s> for <s>Śanaiścara</s> (Saturn), <s>Kāladūti</s> for <s>Rāhu</s>, and <s>Citragupta</s> for <s>Ketu</s> — these are the planetary deities. <s>Agni</s>, the Waters, Earth, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Indrāṇī</s>, <s>Prajāpati</s>, the Serpent, and <s>Brahman</s> — these are the sub-deities (<s>pratyadhidevatā</s>). The Sun is born in <s>Kaliṅga</s>, and the Moon in the <s>Yamunā</s> region;

children.text: nādiśettapasā yuktaṃ nādiśeddivamāśritam /
children.translated_text: [The planets] do not afflict one devoted to <s>tapas</s> (austerity), nor one who has resorted to heaven,

children.text: na ca vedāntakaṃ vipraṃ vṛttāntāṃ nārīṃ parivṛtām //
children.translated_text: nor a <s>vipra</s> (brāhmaṇa) who has mastered <s>Vedānta</s>, nor a virtuous woman who is secluded.

children.text: ahiṃsakasya dāntasya dharmajighanasya ca /
children.translated_text: For one who is non-violent, self-controlled, and devoted to <s>dharma</s>,

children.text: nityaṃ ca niyamasthasya sadānugrahā grahāḥ //
children.translated_text: and who is ever established in discipline (<s>niyama</s>) — the planets are always favorable.

children.text: grahā gāvo narendrāśca brāhmaṇāśca viśeṣataḥ /
children.translated_text: Planets, cows, kings, and <s>brāhmaṇas</s> especially —

children.text: pūjitāḥ pūjayantyete nirdahantyavamānitā // JaimGS_2.9 //
children.translated_text: when worshipped, they honor in return; when disrespected, they destroy. // <s>JaimGS</s> 2.9 //

children.text: // iti jaiminisūtraṃ samāptam //
children.translated_text: // Thus the <s>Jaimini Sūtra</s> is concluded. //
